title: Robert Kiyosaki Urges Buyers to Wait Out the Crash as Bitcoin Plummets
summary: Robert Kiyosaki urged bitcoin buyers to wait until the crash ends as falling prices renewed his interest in buying more. He recalled buying bitcoin at $20,000 per coin after an earlier downturn and said he would wait for another bottom. Kiyosaki Says Wait for the Crash to End Bitcoin’s sell-off brou...
content:
Robert Kiyosaki urged bitcoin buyers to wait until the crash ends as falling prices renewed his interest in buying more. He recalled buying bitcoin at $20,000 per coin after an earlier downturn and said he would wait for another bottom.

Key Takeaways

  • Robert Kiyosaki advised waiting for the bitcoin crash to end before buying.
  • He said he began buying at $20,000 per bitcoin after the last crash.
  • Bitcoin’s 21 million supply limit remains central to his interest.

Kiyosaki Says Wait for the Crash to End

Bitcoin’s sell-off brought market timing into focus for Robert Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poor Dad. On Nov. 20, he urged buyers to wait for the crash to end before purchasing more bitcoin. His warning against buying during the crash on X accompanied plans to buy when he believes the market has reached a bottom.

“Never grab a falling knife,” the famous author wrote, describing the risk of buying into a falling market. He added:

“That means wait for the crash to end… before buying.”

Earlier that day, Kiyosaki described declines in gold, silver, and bitcoin while expressing particular interest in BTC’s drop. In his comments on falling asset prices, he contrasted sellers with people waiting to buy, writing:

“CRASH: good or bad? Gold, silver, bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy? I am most excited about bitcoin’s crash. Waiting to buy more.”

Selling across cryptocurrency markets took bitcoin below $56K. The broader decline produced $2.54 billion in marketwide liquidations over the 24 hours through early Nov. 21. Positions betting on higher prices accounted for $2.27 billion of that total.

Bitcoin changed hands at $59,965 as of 8:38 p.m. EST on Nov. 21, up 1.87% over 24 hours. The price ranged between a low near $55K and a high near $60,660 before slipping back below $60K. BTC last hit $20K in 2023.

Why Does He Want More Bitcoin?

Kiyosaki tied his interest in buying more to bitcoin’s fixed supply, describing roughly 20 million coins as already mined. Bitcoin’s 21 million coin supply limit follows from its issuance schedule: the amount awarded to miners falls by half about every four years. Under current rules, new coin issuance is expected to end around 2140.

Acknowledging uncertainty about the result of buying more during a decline, the renowned author continued:

“With price of bitcoin crashing, I can’t wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a ‘nothing burger’ … or the best money I’ve ever spent.”

Kiyosaki also criticized the Federal Reserve, banks and bond markets while pointing to growing U.S. debt. The Treasury defines public debt outstanding and its components as the principal amount of Treasury securities in circulation. He viewed bitcoin’s limited issuance as a reason to buy despite the turbulence he described.

What Did He Say About Earlier Purchases?

Kiyosaki pointed to an earlier purchase to illustrate why he favors waiting through a decline. The investor recalled: “I began buying bitcoin at $20,000 a coin… after the last crash.” The acclaimed author concluded:

“Will wait for bitcoin bottom again.”

A similar pattern played out in early February, when the author said he was waiting for new price bottoms in gold and bitcoin before adding more. Later that month, he reported picking up one bitcoin at $67,000 as prices fell, citing concerns about U.S. debt and the dollar. His purchases have also come during rallies, at prices well above where bitcoin trades now. In June 2025, he posted that he had bought another bitcoin with the price above $107,000, and in July 2025 he put his latest purchase at $110,000.

On Nov. 4, Kiyosaki said he had added bitcoin, gold and silver while other investors reacted to falling prices. He again connected those purchases to concerns about growing debt and government-issued money, themes he returned to in his latest comments.

title: Bitcoin Mining Profits Turn Ugly Despite Hashrate’s Return Above 1 ZH/s
summary: After shedding roughly 100 exahash per second (EH/s) in computational power, while bitcoin’s price retreated to levels last witnessed during the first week of September 2024, Bitcoin’s hashrate has rebounded decisively, reclaiming the 1,000 EH/s threshold, equivalent to 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s)...
content:
After shedding roughly 100 exahash per second (EH/s) in computational power, while bitcoin’s price retreated to levels last witnessed during the first week of September 2024, Bitcoin’s hashrate has rebounded decisively, reclaiming the 1,000 EH/s threshold, equivalent to 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s) of processing power.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s hashrate has reclaimed the 1 ZH/s zone despite mounting financial pressure across the mining industry with bitcoin’s price tapping a two year low.
  • Historically weak mining revenue and dwindling transaction fees are raising questions about the sustainability of current operations.
  • An approaching difficulty adjustment could introduce fresh economic challenges for miners already navigating an unforgiving market.

Financial Breathing Room Gets Thin for Bitcoin Miners

Bitcoin’s price has endured a punishing stretch, with the world’s largest crypto asset by market capitalization tumbling to $55,081 on Bitstamp on Saturday. The price decline has dealt another significant blow to bitcoin miners, with revenue once again plumbing extreme lows as hashprice slips below $28 per petahash per second (PH/s) of daily computational output.

On Nov. 21, hashprice fell to a low of $26.16 per petahash per second (PH/s) per day, according to hashrateindex.com. Bitcoin miners have found little financial relief in transaction fees, with annual fee revenue tracking toward its lowest level since at least 2011.

Over the past 24 hours, fees accounted for a meager 0.64% of total block rewards, representing considerably less than 1% of miners’ total earnings. Consequently, mining operations remain heavily dependent on bitcoin’s market price, leaving their revenue particularly vulnerable to sharp fluctuations in the asset’s valuation.

American cryptocurrency entrepreneur Kyle Chassé offered a sobering assessment of the state of bitcoin mining to his 283,900 followers on X, observing that “bitcoin is now trading below what it costs to mine.” Drawing a comparison to the economics of precious metals extraction, Chassé added, “Think of a gold mine where every ounce sells for less than it cost to dig.”

“Miners in that spot have two options. Switch machines off, or sell coins to pay the bills. Hashrate is still sitting near record highs. Nobody has switched off yet.”

Chassé concluded with a pointed question that captures the financial predicament confronting the mining industry:

“So who blinks first, the miners or the price?”

Heavyweight ASIC Machines and Lightweight Profits

The financial strain becomes even more apparent when examining what today’s most advanced SHA-256 mining machines actually earn. At an electricity rate of $0.10 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), even newer hydro-cooled models are scraping by on surprisingly thin estimated daily profits. Consider Bitmain’s Antminer S23 Hydro 3U, which produces 1.16 PH/s of computational power yet generates an estimated profit of just $6.29 per day under current market conditions.

The figures become even less encouraging further down the list. Bitdeer’s Sealminer A4 Ultra Hydro (886 TH/s) and Bitmain’s Antminer S23 XP Hyd (600 TH/s) produce estimated daily profits of $4.92 and $4.12, respectively. Meanwhile, other machines operating between 318 TH/s and 865 TH/s are left with estimated daily profits ranging from a mere $0.58 to $3.66, and those figures exclude additional operating expenses.

For miners investing thousands of dollars in specialized equipment, meager returns like these illustrate just how unforgiving the economics of bitcoin mining have become in 2026.

Bitcoin Hashrate Rebounds, but Can Miners Afford to Keep Going?

Despite the financial strain and diminished earnings during the third week of November, bitcoin miners have managed to propel the network’s computational power back above the 1 ZH/s threshold. At press time, Bitcoin’s total hashrate stands at 1.06483 ZH/s. The rise follows an extreme downturn below the 1,000 EH/s range when the hashrate slipped to around 912 EH/s on Nov. 14.

The move was preceded by a 9.13% difficulty reduction, which gave miners a good boost. However, with roughly a week remaining before the next difficulty adjustment, those recent gains could prove short-lived. The next adjustment is expected on or around Nov. 27, 2026, with current estimates pointing to an 8.99% increase in mining difficulty. The projected increase stems from Bitcoin’s block intervals running considerably faster than the network’s intended 10-minute average.

Although the estimate remains subject to change, blocks are currently being discovered every 9 minutes and 10 seconds on average. Bitcoin’s hashrate recovery offers little reassurance when viewed against the broader financial pressures confronting miners. A network reclaiming computational power while operators grapple with dwindling earnings hardly shows a mining industry with sound financial health.

At such depressed hashprices, miners are undoubtedly relying on sunk investments, existing capital reserves or sheer optimism to sustain operations. Even their bitcoin reserves are dwindling, leaving miners with fewer financial resources to withstand an increasingly unforgiving economic environment.

title: AI Finds Bitcoin Core Security Flaw That Could Temporarily Freeze Nodes
summary: Bitcoin Core disclosed a medium-severity vulnerability on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, that allowed malicious peers to temporarily paralyze nodes through repeated transaction announcements. The flaw, discovered through artificial intelligence-assisted security research, highlights how automated vulnerabil...
content:
Bitcoin Core disclosed a medium-severity vulnerability on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, that allowed malicious peers to temporarily paralyze nodes through repeated transaction announcements. The flaw, discovered through artificial intelligence-assisted security research, highlights how automated vulnerability detection is transforming cryptocurrency software security.

Key Takeaways

  • A newly disclosed Bitcoin Core vulnerability raises fresh questions about the resilience of critical network infrastructure.
  • Artificial intelligence is uncovering security weaknesses that escaped years of conventional software scrutiny.
  • The growing sophistication of automated vulnerability research is forcing cryptocurrency developers to reconsider how quickly security threats are addressed.

The vulnerability, cataloged as CVE-2026-117348 and titled “Node stall through duplicate orphan announcements,” could prevent affected Bitcoin nodes from processing incoming blocks and transactions for more than a dozen seconds per malicious message.

According to the official Bitcoin Core disclosure, the problem affected versions 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4, and 31.0 through 31.2. Corrective updates are available in versions 30.5, 31.3, and 32.1, while the discontinued 29.x branch will receive no further patches.

How an AI Scanner Uncovered Bitcoin Core’s Node-Stalling Vulnerability

The software development team known as Bitcoin Core maintains a temporary holding area known as the “orphanage,” where transactions await missing parent transactions. When another network participant announces one of these transactions, the software examines its dependencies to determine which missing information should be requested.

The vulnerability exploited an overlooked inefficiency in that process. Bitcoin inventory messages can contain 50,000 entries, yet the software failed to disregard duplicate transaction announcements. An attacker could repeatedly reference an orphan transaction with thousands of missing parents, forcing the receiving node to perform the same computationally expensive checks thousands of times.

Each manipulated message could stall processing for more than 12 seconds, leaving the targeted node temporarily unable to handle incoming blocks or other network communications.

The discovery originated with Project Loupe, an automated large language model (LLM) security initiative developed by Elias Rohrer at Spiral, Block’s open-source Bitcoin development division. Bitcoin Core developer Gregory Sanders subsequently validated the finding and brought it to the project’s security team.

Project Loupe reported the vulnerability on July 8. An independent researcher identified as Stutxo submitted a separate report on Aug. 4, the same day Sanders opened a corrective pull request. Developers merged the fix on Aug. 6, and Bitcoin Core 32.1 incorporated it on Oct. 27.

The Nov. 20 disclosure accompanied updated releases for maintained older branches. The correction ensures each unique transaction announcement is processed only once per inventory message.

Although the flaw permitted temporary denial-of-service attacks, the advisory did not establish any mechanism for stealing bitcoin or permanently damaging nodes.

AI Security Research Exposes Long-Standing Blockchain Weaknesses

The disclosure arrives amid an extraordinary year for AI-assisted vulnerability research across cryptocurrency infrastructure.

In February, an AI-assisted review identified a critical signature-verification weakness in the XRP Ledger’s proposed Batch amendment before activation. Another investigation uncovered a high-severity vulnerability in Nethermind, an Ethereum execution client, potentially affecting validator operations.

By late May, researcher Taylor Hornby had used an AI-assisted auditing system to identify a four-year-old flaw in Zcash’s Orchard privacy protocol. The vulnerability could have permitted undetectable counterfeit ZEC, although developers corrected it before public disclosure.

August brought another striking demonstration. Sixteen volunteer developers participating in a Bitcoin security initiative generated 4,962 findings across 390 projects in approximately one day, including 85 initially classified as critical.

However, automated discovery introduced considerable complications. Maintainers faced thousands of reports requiring human verification, while legitimate security concerns competed with false positives and poorly substantiated findings.

Core Lightning developers also confronted an influx of AI-generated vulnerability reports, ultimately identifying genuine security problems requiring corrective releases.

The implications extend beyond defensive research. Security specialists have raised concerns that malicious actors can employ similar technology to uncover weaknesses in older software, potentially shortening the useful lifespan of traditional security audits.

Bitcoin Core Accelerates Disclosure as AI Changes Security Research

Recognizing this development, Bitcoin Core revised its vulnerability disclosure policy in October. Issues classified as easily discoverable, including weaknesses identifiable through relatively simple LLM-assisted analysis, now receive accelerated public disclosure alongside corrective releases.

CVE-2026-117348 illustrates that approach in practice.

The episode also exposes a difficult security paradox. AI can identify overlooked vulnerabilities faster than conventional research, but its growing accessibility potentially gives attackers comparable capabilities. For open-source cryptocurrency infrastructure, the central challenge is increasingly not merely discovering weaknesses, but validating and correcting them before adversaries exploit the same knowledge.

title: Behind Closed Doors, Central Banks Build a Case for Bitcoin—But With Gold
summary: In conversations behind closed doors, central bank officials explain that these institutions hold gold and don’t want tokenized gold for the exact same reason bitcoin is valuable: self-custody. At least one central bank is already known to hold bitcoin (BTC), while 7% of surveyed central banks said ...
content:
In conversations behind closed doors, central bank officials explain that these institutions hold gold and don’t want tokenized gold for the exact same reason bitcoin is valuable: self-custody. At least one central bank is already known to hold bitcoin (BTC), while 7% of surveyed central banks said they were considering digital assets in both 2025 and 2026.

Key Takeaways

  • Central banks increasingly see gold held in foreign vaults as a geopolitical risk, reinforcing the case for self-custody.
  • While central banks largely dismiss tokenized gold, at least one has invested in a $1 million bitcoin test portfolio.
  • Bitcoin and gold both offer alternatives to assets held by intermediaries, but bitcoin also offers the potential for direct digital payments.

OMFIF, a London-based forum for central banks, held four meetings this year to discuss gold, resulting in a report based on conversations behind closed doors that was published this week. The findings on surveyed central banks’ interest in investing in digital assets were published in June, while the November report adds further insights relevant to bitcoin adoption.

Since Russia’s reserves were frozen in 2022, central banks have become more aware that an asset held in someone else’s vault isn’t really theirs. The part of Russia’s gold reserves kept inside Russia was not frozen.

Your Asset You Can’t Use

“The frozen reserves have not lost their value, they have lost their utility,” writes Steven Feldman, chief executive of Gold Bullion International, one of the report’s partners. According to him, reserves used to be judged by what they yielded, but are now “also judged by who can say no.”

In other words, this is close to the rule many bitcoiners keep preaching: not your keys, not your coins.

According to the report, an unnamed European central bank sees the concentration of much of its gold in London as a real risk, and has discussed moving some of it elsewhere in Europe. Another European central bank said it keeps about half its gold at home. A European central bank also said the dollar is “now within the geopolitical risk framework rather than being a neutral asset,” while another resumed gold buying after a long pause, “following political enquiries.”

Central Banks Move Gold Closer to Home

Some of these moves are already public. In September, the Dutch central bank said it had moved about 86 tonnes of gold out of New York and Ottawa to London, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest” and saying gold held at the Bank of England is the quickest to deploy in a crisis.

It sold about 59 tonnes in New York and bought gold in London. It also physically moved more than 27 tonnes from the U.S. and Canada to its vault in Zeist, Netherlands, while sending a similar amount from Zeist to London. The share of its gold held at home remained almost 31%.

The Banque de France replaced 129 tonnes it held in New York with gold now stored in Paris. Germany’s Bundesbank, which keeps 1,236 tonnes at the New York Fed, says it has no doubts about the Fed’s reliability.

In its previous gold report, published in 2024, OMFIF quoted a “prominent European central banker” who voiced personal skepticism about gold but said there weren’t many ways to escape the dollar, adding that “gold is one of them along with commodities and crypto assets like bitcoin.”

No to Tokenized Gold

Owning gold directly and relying less on third-parties is the main reason why central banks don’t want tokenized gold. None of the central banks in the working group reported holding or using it.

As a European central bank put it, gold “must be an asset that can be owned and accessed directly,” while tokenized gold depends on its issuers and operators, which can fail or block access to it. Another European central bank emphasized that physical gold offers protection if the current market infrastructure breaks. Gold in a vault “would remain usable without the London fixing, counterparties, or online infrastructure.”

Bitcoin Can Be Stolen, So Can Gold

This is also where gold has some advantages over not only its tokenized counterpart but also “digital gold”—bitcoin. Bitcoin largely depends on online infrastructure and introduces cybersecurity threats, as hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin were stolen from self-custodial wallets this year.

Such risks can be mitigated, for example, with multisig setups—although AI-assisted criminals, in theory, may eventually find ways to compromise them as well. Similarly, physical gold vaults can also be targets of theft or seizure.

Far more gold has been lost to those controlling the vault than to burglars. One of the largest gold robberies on record, the 1983 Brink’s-Mat raid at Heathrow, involved the theft of about 3 tonnes of a bullion bank’s gold. Meanwhile, in late 1940, Vichy France agreed to hand Nazi Germany the 198 tonnes of gold that Belgium had entrusted to the Banque de France. Now, central banks are again rethinking where they keep their gold as geopolitical tensions rise.

One Bank Is In, 70+ to Go

However, for now, the report—which has several major global gold market players among its partners—largely dismisses bitcoin as an alternative.

OMFIF’s report shows that 92% of surveyed central banks don’t invest in digital assets, 7% are considering them, and 1% already invest. The Czech National Bank, which bought a $1 million test portfolio of bitcoin, a dollar stablecoin, and a tokenized deposit in November 2025, is one example of a central bank investing in digital assets. The portfolio is held outside its official reserves.

OMFIF said it surveyed 74 central banks for the 2026 report. In its 2025 survey, 7% of the 75 surveyed banks also said they were considering investing in digital assets. However, it’s unknown whether the Czech central bank was among those considering investments in 2025 or whether another bank has since joined the group.

As reported by Bitcoin.com News, in March 2026, the National Bank of Kazakhstan said it would establish a portfolio of up to $350 million in crypto asset companies and other instruments offering exposure to digital assets, funded from gold and part of its foreign reserves.

What’s more, in OMFIF’s 2026 survey, 13% of central banks expected to increase their unspecified digital asset allocations over the next 10 years, up from 10% a year earlier.

Private Gold Buyers Outpace Central Banks

The fact that at least one European central bank has invested in bitcoin could already be considered a significant achievement for an asset that is still relatively young.

Meanwhile, in 2026, the World Gold Council says central banks added 321 tonnes in the third quarter, up 42% year over year, bringing purchases for the first nine months to 675 tonnes—6% more than in the same period of 2025.

Savers have been buying more gold than central banks. Last year, bar and coin demand reached 1,374 tonnes ($154 billion), while central banks added 863 tonnes. In the third quarter of 2026, however, central banks bought more gold (321 tonnes) than bar and coin buyers (268 tonnes).

Alexej Jordanov of Gold Republic, one of the report’s partners, writes that every year since 2010, private savers have bought more gold in bars and coins than central banks have added to their reserves, purchasing about twice as much overall.

“Gradually, one gram at a time, they are becoming their own central banks,” Jordanov writes, adding that a gold bar held in one’s own name “leaves no one between the owner and the metal.” This is similar to how you might keep bitcoin in self-custody rather than hold an ETF share.

Risky Insurance and Safe Havens

Matthew Ferranti of the University of Cincinnati’s Cryptoeconomics Lab, a research fellow at the Bitcoin Policy Institute (recently rebranded the Finney Foundation for Open Technology), argued in a peer-reviewed paper published in 2025 that gold and bitcoin both work as insurance against sanctions for a central bank, with gold doing so only if it sits in the central bank’s own vault.

In an article published by the Foundation in January, Ferranti found that bitcoin’s price rose when the odds of Jerome Powell’s removal as Fed chair increased, suggesting bitcoin may also protect against a loss of Federal Reserve independence.

In any case, both gold and bitcoin fell this year, with both supposed safe havens behaving like risk assets during the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis. However, while bitcoin initially fell, it later outperformed gold for weeks.

All that said, both gold and bitcoin offer the ability to hold assets without intermediaries, especially during periods of rising uncertainty. Both assets have their own advantages, downsides, and risks, and can serve different user profiles.

Central banks also appear to be warming up to the idea of holding bitcoin in their reserves, albeit slowly. This would give them the opportunity not only to hold it but also to use it, e.g., for payments—something that would be much more complicated with gold bars.

Verdict on the Margex Offer

How We Verified These Welcome Bonus Offers?

We verified these welcome offers by checking the four criteria: offer value, trading volume requirement, expiration, and eligible regions.

  • Offer value: We separated the headline maximum from the amount a normal new user can reach. You see, a package worth 30,000 USDT may include a small sign-up reward, but a much larger futures tier for high-volume traders. We also checked whether the reward comes as withdrawable crypto, a fee rebate, a mystery box, a trading bonus, or a trial fund.
  • Trading Volume requirement: We compared the required net deposit with the spot or futures volume needed for each tier. Plus, we also checked common exclusions such as internal transfers, zero-fee trades, API activity, bot volume, and subaccounts.
  • Duration: We checked how long you have to finish a task, claim a completed reward, and use the claimed voucher. You see, every crypto exchange sign-up bonus has an expiry date, generally within 30 days of registration.
  • Eligible regions: We compared the campaign country rules with each exchange’s current restricted-location terms. A referral link may open in your browser even though your verified country cannot join the offer. We also treated U.S. versions of Binance and OKX as separate services because their global bonuses and products do not automatically carry over.

Are crypto sign-up bonuses worth it?

Yes, crypto sign-up bonuses are genuinely worth claiming in most cases, as long as you go in with realistic expectations about what you’ll actually receive. 

The instant, low-effort tiers, like Binance’s KYC voucher or even Margex’s flat $50, cost you basically nothing beyond a few minutes of setup. But again, the bigger headline numbers, like Bybit’s $30,020 or MEXC’s $10,000, require serious capital and trading volume that most casual users will never reach, so you should treat those as aspirational rather than expected.

You see, no-deposit bonus offers are rare, and a free crypto sign-up bonus with instant withdrawal usually comes with a lock, KYC step, or trading condition. The better way is to value a bonus at what you can personally use. Also, most of the bonus funds usually arrive as trading credit or vouchers rather than withdrawable cash. Hence, at least at first, read the terms before assuming you can cash out immediately.

Which crypto exchange sign-up bonus is the best for your trading type?

The best crypto sign-up bonus, or welcome reward, depends more on how you plan to use the exchange. According to the definition of crypto welcome bonus, the first-time account openers may benefit more from simple deposit or first-trade rewards, while buy-and-hold investors should look for those bonuses that never require heavy trading, and frequent traders often get more from fee discounts and similar exchange promotions.

Next, high-frequency and grid traders can usually get more value from trading-fee rebates, volume-based sign-up rewards, and futures bonuses because they trade more often.

First-Time Account Openers

First-time account openers should choose a bonus with very simple requirements and a low minimum deposit. You know, a reward for completing KYC, making your first deposit, or placing a few trades makes more sense than a large bonus that requires thousands of dollars in trading volume. Hence, you should mainly focus on how easy the reward is to unlock rather than its maximum advertised value.

Buy-and-Hold Investors

Buy-and-hold investors should look for deposit bonuses or rewards that require little trading. Basically, a $50 reward after depositing and buying crypto can be more useful than a $500 futures bonus that requires active trading. Plus, you should also avoid promotions that force you to generate high trading volume because frequent buying and selling does not match a long-term investment strategy.

High-Frequency and Grid Traders

High-frequency and grid traders can benefit most from bonuses linked to trading volume. Here, fee rebates, futures credits, trading vouchers, and volume-based rewards become more valuable because you naturally place many trades. Hence, a bonus with a higher trading requirement may therefore make sense for you, provided the normal trading fees and conditions remain competitive.

Are free crypto sign-up bonuses available for every exchange?

No, free crypto sign-up bonuses are not available on every exchange. Not every platform uses the same signup structure, and some reserve free bitcoin or similar promotions for app-based campaigns or limited regions. Basically, each platform decides its own promotion rules, and some exchanges do not offer any reward just for creating an account.

Even exchanges that advertise a welcome bonus usually ask you to complete certain steps first. So, you may need to verify your identity, deposit a minimum amount, make your first trade, or reach a required trading volume. The reward can also vary by country, campaign period, and referral link.

Can I withdraw my free crypto bonuses immediately?

No, you cannot withdraw a free crypto bonus immediately, as most exchanges place conditions on the reward because the bonus is meant to encourage real trading activity, not simply give away withdrawable cash.

You should also check the exchange app terms carefully, since bonuses can vary by region and some platforms use promotions to grow their user base.

You may need to deposit funds, complete KYC, make a certain number of trades, or reach a required trading volume before the bonus even becomes eligible for withdrawal. Plus, some rewards cannot be withdrawn at all. So, for example, futures bonuses and trading credits may only cover trading losses or fees, while you can withdraw the profits earned from them under certain rules.

Of course, this works differently from exchange to exchange. Hence, you should always check the withdrawal terms first, especially the minimum trading requirement, expiry date, and whether the bonus itself or only the profits can be withdrawn.

title: Bitcoin Proof-of-Work Can Help Stop AI Cyberattacks: Ex-Space Force Director
summary: Major Jason Lowery, author of the Softwar thesis, has proposed using the proof-of-work consensus mechanism that secures bitcoin to defend key U.S. digital property against artificial intelligence-led threats, which are already affecting financial institutions and government agencies. Jason Lowery Pr...
content:
1. News
  2. Security
  3. Bitcoin Proof-of-Work Can Help Stop AI Cyberattacks: Ex-Space Force Director

Published:Nov 21, 2026, 4:25 PM EST

Major Jason Lowery, author of the Softwar thesis, has proposed using the proof-of-work consensus mechanism that secures bitcoin to defend key U.S. digital property against artificial intelligence-led threats, which are already affecting financial institutions and government agencies.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 21, 2026, 4:25 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Major Jason Lowery suggested using Bitcoin’s proof-of-work to secure US infrastructure against AI attacks.
  • The system would require massive energy expenditure to process commands, making cyberattacks cost-prohibitive.
  • This proposal follows recent cyberattacks on US agencies and the firing of the National Cyber Director.

Jason Lowery Proposes Using Proof of Work to Defend Against AI

Bitcoin’s proof-of-work (PoW) consensus mechanism, which has often been criticized for being energy intensive and wasteful, might have a role to play in the upcoming battle against cyberattacks carried out by artificial intelligence agents.

Major Jason Lowery, former deputy director of technology & innovation at the U.S. Space Force and now special assistant to the commander at the U.S. Pacific Command, has hinted at the use of Bitcoin’s network as a security element that could help to deal with ongoing threats.

After being absent from social media for some time and deleting almost all of his previous messages, Lowery suggested implementing Bitcoin-backed measures to counter these dangers.

“I am ready and willing to support this country with using Bitcoin’s PoW network to counter the threat of agentic superintelligence. This has been the singular focus of my life since 2021,” he stated.

Lowery, who has discussed bitcoin’s relevance as a geopolitical defense element, is the author of Softwar, a thesis that promotes bitcoin not as an alternative monetary system, but as a power projection protocol that can be used to secure critical infrastructure and raise the physical costs of an attack.

While Lowery did not specify how bitcoin’s proof-of-work consensus could be implemented to this end, Softwar explains that the most effective way to constrain a computer involves imposing physical costs for each action, requiring each instruction to spend large energy resources.

Implementing Lowery’s proof-of-work shield—which Softwar describes as the “Electronic Cyber Dome” defense framework—on key security infrastructure and information would reject any signals (attacks) that don’t also include proof-of-work stamps.

To access key elements, an agent would have to spend more electricity than the defense surrounding it, making defense infinitely scalable through power increases and hardware investments. That would make attacks on critical setups as costly as the government wanted them to be, relying on already available proof-of-stake networks.

Lowery’s proposal comes after President Donald Trump fired National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross for not being “good enough” as U.S. agencies and financial institutions face a wave of cyberattacks that threaten to hit key state functions. On Thursday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture was hit with a cyberattack, reportedly affecting Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping, payments, and contracting.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) was also reportedly hit by a cyberattack that breached its National Crime Information Center, a database used by law enforcement at a federal and state level to identify wanted fugitives and check for outstanding warrants.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: In GTA VI You Can Steal Anything Except Your Own Copy.
summary: Rockstar’s return to Vice City is an extraordinary crime game, a surprisingly good love story, and a lesson in what passes for ownership in 2026, delivered alongside an estimated US$3.79 billion in launch-day sales.
content:
Skip to content

Rockstar’s return to Vice City is an extraordinary crime game, a surprisingly good love story, and a lesson in what passes for ownership in 2026, delivered alongside an estimated US$3.79 billion in launch-day sales.

In Grand Theft Auto VI, the drug dealers worry about Instagram. As The Guardian’s Keza MacDonald put it in her review, “even the narcos are obsessed with their Instagram clout.” In the original Vice City, Rockstar gave us the Scarface fantasy of a man doing cocaine at a desk large enough to land a helicopter on. In 2026, the same man would have to angle the desk for the light and spend Tuesday afternoon explaining to his associates why they need to post more consistently. The reach has been disappointing.

GTA VI launched on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, thirteen years after GTA V. Rockstar’s day-one figures filed with the SEC put estimated worldwide retail sales through the end of November 19 at US$3.79 billion. Rockstar separately reported 32.5 million copies sold before release. The company also put GTA V at nearly 235 million units sold into retail and distribution. That’s the commercial inheritance behind the richest irony of launch week. Rockstar built a Florida where you can steal a car, take it wherever you like, and abandon it in a swamp. Buy the game in a box and once you’ve used the code, the only thing left to lend a friend is the box.

Vice City, now with people in it

The 2002 Vice City was an ’80s Miami mixtape with a body count. The city now sits inside Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional Florida, alongside the Keys, wetlands, malls, flea markets and whole stretches of road you might follow just to see where they go. Map size is the easiest thing here to oversell. Anyone can make a big map and scatter errands over it until it resembles the home screen of a phone you desperately need to clean out. Rockstar makes it tempting to miss your turn on purpose.

During a demonstration for The Guardian, Jason petted a stranger’s dog, took out binoculars to identify a gull, and added it to a wildlife log. There are 62 kinds of birds to spot. Someone at Rockstar understood that the definitive car-theft simulator needed a gull with absolutely no interest in furthering the plot. The music serves a similar purpose. The original score is by Justice, the French duo who made dance music sound like a leather jacket plugged into the mains. The old Vice City understood that the right song can make a drive more memorable than the mission at the other end. The new one has enough confidence in its world to let you keep driving.

Rockstar Games’ extended look at GTA VI, captured in-game on PlayStation 5.

Bonnie and Clyde need groceries

GTA V gave us three men taking turns embodying different strains of American brain damage. This time it’s Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a couple whose easy score goes bad and who have to decide how much they’re willing to do for each other. There’s a button for holding hands. You can stock the fridge. The Washington Post’s Gene Park, testing how the story responded to neglect, wrote, “I even forced Jason to become a total loser”. He had Jason sleep through picking Lucia up from prison and saw different scenes and arguments. Even in a game that can swallow a hundred hours, the guy with the stolen sports car still has to answer a question familiar to anyone who’s ever dated a man with a car. Where the hell were you?

Rockstar’s Rob Nelson told The Guardian the team wanted to “provide mechanisms that encourage empathy”. That sounds like what Pixar might put on a slide for investors. Here it shows up in what the game lets you do. Park describes jobs that can end without a shot fired and a night out where introducing your girlfriend to your repellent friends is an actual social problem to solve. Giving you a reason to care what happens after the shooting makes the violence a little less disposable.

Lucia has room to be ruthless, funny, horny and vulnerable, sometimes within the same stretch of the story. MacDonald noticed the difference in the women around her, too, from the rappers trying to make it to the middle-aged drug runner with a beloved purple rifle. There are male strippers. After several decades of debate over the male gaze, Rockstar has worked out that a man can also take his trousers off and disappoint a room full of people.

The increased realism also invites a kind of low-grade domestic misery. Park reports that neglecting food and sleep can hurt a job, and that people notice when you go too long without a shower. MacDonald tried to say hello to a stranger and punched him instead. Some of that friction produces stories you actually want to tell. Some of it sounds like a very expensive way to have a fitness tracker and a parole officer agree about your lifestyle. And the old frat-house writing still turns up in the form of horny pensioners on TV and a golf-club gag about testicles. The sharper the human observation gets, the more those jokes sound like a guy who’s been invited back to the writers’ room because his dad owns the building.

The box is yours. Enjoy the box.

As BNC reported when pre-orders opened, the standard edition costs US$79.99, the Ultimate Edition costs US$99.99, and the boxed standard edition comes with a download code in place of a disc. PC players sat out launch day. The code is the more interesting bit. A disc could circulate among friends or end up on a used-game shelf. A redeemed code leaves you with a handsome piece of shelf decoration. The industry has spent years persuading people that a purchase and an account entitlement are interchangeable. Now it puts the entitlement in a box and lets your childhood do the rest of the marketing.

Downloads are convenient. Nobody particularly misses getting up to switch discs. The point of the box is that it preserves the appearance of a transaction whose terms have changed. Sony and Microsoft can deliver a game to your couch in the middle of the night. Your friend still can’t borrow the one you paid for by picking it up off the coffee table. Apparently the future of retail needed a prop department.

The same pre-order window attracted GTA-themed memecoins and unauthorized sites offering fake early access for crypto. If you remember Snoop Dogg selling almost a million Telegram collectibles, you already know how efficiently a recognizable name can move a digital object. What’s funny about the GTA knockoffs is how little of the original business they needed to imitate. A logo, a checkout and the promise of getting in before everyone else will take you surprisingly far. The official business was already good at selling things that cost very little to duplicate. Take-Two reported that recurrent consumer spending, its category for virtual currency, add-ons and similar purchases, accounted for 81% of companywide net revenue in the quarter ended September 30. Rockstar offered a free month of GTA+ with digital pre-orders. Even the satire of hustle culture had a subscription trial at checkout.

Tony Montana would have a discount code

Vice City is American, but its understanding of status travels. In October, Pew Research Center found that one in five American adults regularly got news from TikTok, rising to 39% among adults aged 18 to 29. People all over the West know the experience of opening the same feed for election results, watching somebody accuse the winner of cheating, then discovering the accuser has a discount code for powdered greens. The phone has one set of tools for working out what’s true, becoming famous and shifting inventory. Rockstar’s narcos have grasped that arrangement as well as any lifestyle entrepreneur with a lav mic. Their genuine competitive advantage is that they know they’re criminals.

What makes VI interesting is that Rockstar could have simply cashed in on all that recognition. It has instead made a game where a little time spent with another person can matter as much as your next big score. For a weekend at least, it also gave people who live in incompatible feeds something to talk about besides what their feeds had just told them to hate. There’s real pleasure in that, even if the entertainment industry will study the launch and conclude the secret ingredient was a familiar logo and a hundred-dollar edition.

Rockstar has made a place where you can get away with an incredible amount and occasionally choose to be decent. It sold that place to millions of people who used to hand a game to a friend and say, “You have to try this.” Somewhere between the gull, the hand-holding button and the empty box, somebody put a hell of a lot of work into remembering how people behave. Somebody else figured out how to bill both friends.

title: Bitcoin Miners Had Fewer Hardware Sellers in 2026 as BTC Tanked and AI Grew
summary: While more companies attempted to challenge Bitmain’s dominance in the Bitcoin mining hardware market, these efforts—which are relevant to Bitcoin’s resilience—now appear to be on pause. Bitmain’s challengers have either stopped selling to external clients or sharply reduced sales. While mining pool...
content:
While more companies attempted to challenge Bitmain’s dominance in the Bitcoin mining hardware market, these efforts—which are relevant to Bitcoin’s resilience—now appear to be on pause. Bitmain’s challengers have either stopped selling to external clients or sharply reduced sales.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitmain and MicroBT dominate Bitcoin mining hardware as rival manufacturers scale back external sales.
  • AI demand and weak mining profitability have pushed Bitdeer, Velaura AI, and Canaan to shift priorities.
  • While this concentration persists, so do the associated centralization risks.

While mining pool concentration is the most frequently cited concern about mining centralization, a more diversified hardware market would also make Bitcoin more resilient. However, those looking to enter this business now have fewer options when choosing new machines.

For example, Bitdeer has put large-scale external sales on hold and uses almost all of its rigs for its own mining. Velaura AI (formerly Auradine) has shifted its focus to AI chips, and Canaan’s rig sales fell 96% year over year in Q3 as it turned toward energy projects. Meanwhile, Block’s Proto lost its only major named buyer. Therefore, miners looking for new rigs today have mostly Bitmain and MicroBT to choose from, leaving those seeking non-Chinese hardware with limited options.

The Mining Oligopoly

According to the latest available data from the Cambridge Digital Mining Industry Report, gathered in June 2024, Bitmain held 82% of the market. Together with the next two largest players, it controlled more than 99%. The data was based on a survey of 46 mining firms that collectively accounted for up to 48% of the Bitcoin network’s hashrate, or computational power.

Cambridge describes this hardware market as highly oligopolistic. Such concentration means that if something goes wrong with one manufacturer, then a large share of the network’s machines could be affected. For example, the outcome of a U.S. national security investigation into Bitmain remains unknown. Bloomberg reported in November 2025 that a Department of Homeland Security-led probe was examining whether Bitmain machines could be accessed remotely for spying or to disrupt the U.S. power grid. Bitmain has denied posing any risk to U.S. national security.

Also, Bitdeer, which was spun off from Bitmain in 2021, manufactures its chips at TSMC in Taiwan. Bitmain has reportedly used TSMC as well, while the foundry is already operating at full capacity due to the expansion of the AI industry.

Bitcoin Bears, AI Bulls

Efforts to diversify the bitcoin mining hardware market have stalled this year. Mining generated less revenue per unit of computing power than ever before, while large miners pivoted to AI data centers, reducing demand for bitcoin mining rigs. Meanwhile, chip factories themselves were overwhelmed with orders from the AI industry.

For example, the so-called hashprice, or how much a miner can expect to earn per unit of computing power per day, hit an all-time low in June. Publicly listed miners, as a group, also mined below cash breakeven in Q2. According to CoinShares, their average cash cost per bitcoin was about $75,500 in the second quarter, while BTC ended the quarter at a price of $58,400.

When Will Bitdeer Resume Sales?

Meanwhile, with chip factories busy fulfilling AI-related orders, Bitdeer CEO Jihan Wu said in May 2026 that the company was prioritizing its own mining over rig sales, partly because of limited chip fabrication capacity. For Bitdeer, it makes more sense to keep scarce chips for its own mining operations and earn revenue from mining rather than sell the rigs.

“Right now, the bitcoin price is still in its bearish situation, and if we sell the mining rigs, we will have to sell it at a very bad price,” Wu said during an earnings call back then.

In Q3 2026, Bitdeer’s SEALMINER sales revenue fell 97% to $0.3 million, while its average self-mining hashrate increased.

Leo Li, Bitdeer’s U.S. sales director, told Bitcoin.com News that large-scale external sales of its SEALMINERs were currently on hold. The company was prioritizing the deployment of its mining rigs across its self-mining operations and co-mining partnerships.

“We believe this approach allows us to optimize capital allocation and capture greater long-term value from our proprietary mining technology,” Li said, adding that external sales might resume “based on market conditions, production capacity, and our broader business priorities.”

The U.S. sales director confirmed that the “vast majority” of Bitdeer’s active self-mining rigs were powered by SEALMINERs. TSMC remained its only foundry partner.

Pivoting to AI and Falling Sales

Meanwhile, Auradine was the main U.S.-designed alternative to Chinese mining machines. However, in March, the company renamed itself Velaura AI and refocused on AI chips. Chief Strategy Officer Sanjay Gupta told TheEnergyMag at the time that the company would work through its existing inventory, while increasingly using unsold units for its own mining at third-party facilities.

The oldest name in the business, Canaan, earned more from mining bitcoin itself than from selling machines in Q2, and expected hardware sales to decline further. They did in Q3: revenue from product sales dropped 65% from Q2 to $4.8 million, while mining revenue fell 46% to $9.5 million, mainly because Canaan operated fewer of its own machines. The company cited continued weak demand for mining equipment and intense pricing competition.

In its Q3 report, Canaan Chairman and CEO Nangeng Zhang said the company remained focused “on two complementary priorities”—expanding its access to cost-advantaged power resources for mining and compute infrastructure, while also maintaining its core mining hardware technology and bitcoin mining capabilities through “disciplined, commercially driven investment.”

Proto Customer and Bitcoin Deals

Jack Dorsey’s Block entered the Bitcoin mining hardware market in 2024 and launched its modular Proto rigs in 2025. However, its first and biggest named customer, Core Scientific, paid $42 million in 2026 to cancel the remainder of its order as it pivoted to AI data centers. Proto hardware is still reaching buyers, though. Bitcoin.com News reported in October that Bitcoin mining services provider Sazmining had launched an offering that allows individual investors to buy Proto hashboards. Buyers own the hashboards, while Sazmining handles operations and maintenance.

Meanwhile, the biggest name in the business, Bitmain, was also hit by the slump and cut prices to clear inventory in Dec. 2025. However, since at least Dec. 2024, Bitmain has allowed large miners to pay for machines by pledging bitcoin at a fixed price, with the option to buy the BTC back later. Some of its largest disclosed deals were paid for this way, including American Bitcoin’s $314 million deal in 2025.

Bitmain has also had a U.S. production line since Dec. 2024 and announced plans for a larger U.S. site. Bitdeer is building a SEALMINER assembly facility in Nevada, while MicroBT has already begun U.S.-based manufacturing. MicroBT is also a private company and, like Bitmain, does not publish sales results. It continues to release new machines, with its latest model, the M7D, debuting in March this year.

More Open-Source

Therefore, the Bitcoin mining industry still depends mostly on chips designed by Chinese companies Bitmain and MicroBT, as well as Canaan, Singapore-based Bitdeer, and U.S.-based Proto. Meanwhile, even the growing solo mining market mostly runs on Bitmain’s chips.

Beyond these companies, a community-supported initiative called the 256 Foundation is working on alternatives. The public charity says its mission is to build open-source alternatives to every closed layer of the mining stack, including hashboards, control boards and firmware. However, its hashboard—the circuit board that carries the mining chips—uses Bitmain chips. Meanwhile, Proto donated 256,000 Intel mining chips to the foundation, but Intel stopped making these chips in 2023.

This is why Canaan’s decision to release open-source firmware for its Avalon Nano 3S, including the driver for its A3197S mining chip, is a big deal. With this move, Canaan is giving developers and users the ability to inspect, modify, and improve the software themselves without needing permission.

“In our view there’s no downside here for Canaan, only upside. Open firmware brings in developers, tinkerers, and home miners who want to understand and own their machines,” 256 Foundation said, urging other mining hardware makers to do the same.

A Temporary Phase With an Unknown End

All that said, the current situation, with fewer new hardware sellers remaining in the market, might still be temporary. If the price of bitcoin rallies and the AI pivot proves less profitable than expected, then mining could become more attractive again. Demand for rigs could also increase, potentially spurring competition among manufacturers.

Canaan has already said it expects revenue to rise to $18–22 million in Q4 from $14.5 million in Q3, although it did not specify how much would come from rig sales. Also, while there are fewer sellers, the machines actually running on the network are likely more varied than they were a few years ago. Bitdeer now mines mostly with its own chips, as does Velaura AI on a smaller scale, while the latter also sells its inventory.

Additionally, those looking to start mining bitcoin now can consider buying used rigs from miners pivoting to AI. While this does not diversify the hardware market itself, it at least gives prospective miners more purchasing options.

In either case, although the situation may be temporary, no one knows how long the current market oligopoly and its associated risks will last.

title: Bipartisan Attorney General Coalition Fights CFTC Prediction Market Power Grab
summary: The coalition, led by New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, has objected to two CFTC proposed rules that classify sports and election-based event contracts in which participants wager against each other as “swaps,” placing them under the commission’s exclusive oversight. Bipartisan AG Coal...
content:
The coalition, led by New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, has objected to two CFTC proposed rules that classify sports and election-based event contracts in which participants wager against each other as “swaps,” placing them under the commission’s exclusive oversight.

Key Takeaways

  • 44 attorneys general opposed CFTC rules giving the agency exclusive prediction market oversight.
  • The coalition claims the CFTC lacks legal authority, threatening states’ power to regulate gambling.
  • The pushback intensifies ongoing legal battles to force platforms to obey local gambling laws and taxes.

Bipartisan AG Coalition Opposes Rules Reclassifying Some Sports and Election-Based Event Contracts as Swaps

The federal-state conflict over who regulates prediction markets continues, and now states are fighting to prevent the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) from implementing proposed rules that would give the commission exclusive oversight over these platforms.

A bipartisan coalition of 44 attorneys general co-led by New Jersey AG Jennifer Davenport sent objections to two proposed rules that would expand the Commission’s oversight on these platforms, keeping state regulators out of the loop.

The first interim rule, already in effect, acknowledges traditional “casino-house” products as gambling, leaving event markets—where bettors wager against each other—out of this classification. The second rule, which is still proposed, aims to reclassify sports and election event markets as swaps, displacing states’ ability to regulate and license them.

Attorneys general from Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, and Wisconsin, pushed against these proposals, stressing that the CFTC regulates specific financial markets and has no legal power to address the harms that gambling can cause.

In addition, the coalition assesses that the commission lacks the power to enact these rules, going beyond the rulemaking power Congress gave it.

Attorney General Davenport stated that the CFTC “continues to stray far outside of its lane” by claiming exclusive oversight of these forms of gambling in prediction markets.

“These actions seek to override states’ longstanding authority to regulate gambling within our borders, which would allow prediction markets to operate without complying with state gambling regulations and safeguards to ensure responsible gaming,” she concluded.

In July, a 44-state bipartisan coalition of AGs led by Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson sent similar objections to these rules, calling to toss them.

Prediction markets face legal action from several state regulators pushing back against the CFTC’s claims of exclusive oversight, stressing that gambling activities under the companies’ umbrella must be licensed and regulated at the state level, paying the related taxes for their operations.

title: XMR1 Crashes 99.8% After $13.5M Hyperliquid Dump, Wagyu Pledges Full Refunds
summary:
Key Takeaways: Hyperliquid saw $13.51 million withdrawn from its XMR1 holdings, resulting in a drop of nearly 99.8%. Bitquery tracked 5.2 million XMR1 that have been sent from the deployer
The post XMR1 Crashes 99.8% After $13.5M Hyperliquid Dump, Wagyu Pledges Full Refunds appeared first on CryptoN...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Hyperliquid saw $13.51 million withdrawn from its XMR1 holdings, resulting in a drop of nearly 99.8%.
  • Bitquery tracked 5.2 million XMR1 that have been sent from the deployer account prior to dump.
  • Wagyu, it said, has said it will reimburse affected traders following the theft of its deployer key.

Monero’s token XMR1 fell from about $500 to about $1 on Nov. 20th after a new account entered the market with hundreds of thousands of tokens.

Bitquery was able to trace them through Hyperliquid and Arbitrum and Ethereum, while the XMR1’s service Wagyu traced the incident to a misused deployer key.

  • XMR1 Loses 99.8% in About 30 Minutes
  • Attacker Converts USDC Into Thousands of ETH
    • Wagyu Says Deployer Key Was Stolen
    • Monero Was Not the Asset That Failed

XMR1 Loses 99.8% in About 30 Minutes

According to Bitquery’s updated analysis, the XMR1 deployer account transferred 5.2 million tokens to a fresh address in three transactions. In just 30 minutes, the receiving account then attempted to sell 369,623 XMR1 to 420 buyers at an average price of $13.51M, pushing the price of XMR down from around $500 to around $1.

The losses were skewed to larger market players. It turned out that 27 accounts that bought at least $100,000 accounted for 77% of all funding, and 75% of the funds raised were already on the order book.

Attacker Converts USDC Into Thousands of ETH

The XMR1 sales were followed by the on-chain trail. Hyperliquid’s $13.28M of USDC was tracked by Bitquery to Arbitrum.Bitquery located the $13.28M of Hyperliquid’s USDC that was sent to Arbitrum. 0.9% of this $13.22 million was then swapped over from CoW on to 7,467 ETH for the majority of which was subsequently bridged to Ethereum through Socket, Mayan and Stargate.

7,348 ETH were left in three wallets at the time of Bitquery’s latest check. A single wallet held the most with 4,836 ETH and no other transactions were made.

Read More: Anthropic’s $83 IPO Fuels Hyperliquid Bets and Fresh Ether Liquidity Debate Before Nasdaq

Wagyu Says Deployer Key Was Stolen

PerpetualCow, representing Wagyu, claimed that the attackers acquired the XMR1 deployer key after a cyberattack on 1984.hosting, the Icelandic hosting provider.

The hosting company and the national cyber security unit of Iceland made two separate reports regarding a serious cyber security incident. But the transfers were impossible to trace by blockchain data as to whether the deployer key was acquired by accidents or processes, and who handled the key at the time of the transfers.

PerpetualCow has guaranteed to cash out those who’ve lost money and stated that Wagyu will be re-launched.

Monero Was Not the Asset That Failed

This incident involved XMR1 and not an actual Monero (XMR). Since native XMR can’t trade directly there, it’s found on an alternative privacy-focused blockchain which is why XMR1 is present on Hyperliquid as a representation of Monero. Wagyu has an additional bridge to deposit Monero, get XMR to trade with and then convert back to Monero at a later time.

That means the focus on the security is on the token issuance entity, the bridge’s infrastructure, and privileged keys more so than on the Monero system.

Bitquery also discovered that the same deployer account once again held 99.97% of the ZEC1 token used for representing Zcash, meaning another large supply of tokens, this time ZEC1, was under the same key used in the XMR1 transfers.

title: Tether Backs SCRYPT to Scale Institutional Stablecoin Payments Across Global Markets
summary:
Key Takeaways: Tether has staked money in the Swiss stablecoin platform called SCRYPT. This deal is meant for institutional payments, foreign exchange and cross-border settlement. SCRYPT is expected to venture
The post Tether Backs SCRYPT to Scale Institutional Stablecoin Payments Across Global Mark...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tether has staked money in the Swiss stablecoin platform called SCRYPT.
  • This deal is meant for institutional payments, foreign exchange and cross-border settlement.
  • SCRYPT is expected to venture into fiat accounts and third party payments.

Tether has simultaneously signed an agreement to invest in SCRYPT, a Switzerland-based trading and liquidity provider of the institutional sector.

The agreement aims to enable banks, brokers, fintechs, and payment companies to transfer funds from one country to another via stablecoins alongside traditional currency.

  • Tether Targets Institutional Stablecoin Payments
    • Stablecoins Cut Dependence on Prefunded Accounts
  • SCRYPT Expands Beyond Trading and Liquidity
    • Tether Builds a Wider Cross-Border Payment Network

Tether Targets Institutional Stablecoin Payments

Tether said the investment will support SCRYPT’s expansion into third-party payments, building on its existing services for liquidity, foreign exchange and cross-border settlement.

SCRYPT already integrates trading, payments, custody and asset management for fiat currencies, stablecoins and all other digital assets. It provides 24/7 spot trading, OTC trading, Foreign Exchange trading, as well as segregated custody based on multi-party computation on its platform.

The companies didn’t specify the amount of the investment. The main scenario is simple: institutions can convert and deposit fiat assets into stablecoins, and then convert and withdraw their value without factoring in banking hours.

Read More: Tether Fires Back After S&P Keeps USDT at Weakest Stability Score Over Reserve Risks

Stablecoins Cut Dependence on Prefunded Accounts

Often, businesses must maintain multiple payments balances in the markets to be able to settle payments promptly. Tether believes that the ability of stablecoins to easily transfer liquidity across markets, day or night, can mitigate that requirement.

In the case of a payment company, it can unlock cash previously held on those preferences balances. Stablecoin settlement can also improve the time-to-money settlement for enterprises trading across time zones.

The CEO of Tether, Paolo Ardoino, has stated that stablecoins must be interchangeable rather than an alternative financial layer, to make them useful to institutions.

SCRYPT Expands Beyond Trading and Liquidity

Norman Wooding, CEO of SCRYPT, stated that the company will develop infrastructure for institutions adopting stablecoins on a large scale and expand to fiat accounts and payments.

That enables the Tether investment to accomplish far more than merely just growing trading volume for USDT.

The strategy connects stablecoin liquidity with traditional payment rails, allowing banks, fintechs and corporate treasury teams to use digital assets without fully abandoning fiat settlement.

SCRYPT is looking to become a bridge between the two, to offer crypto traders, custodians, FX and payments through one institutional platform.

Tether Builds a Wider Cross-Border Payment Network

The SCRYPT investment comes off the heels of several other Tether payment infrastructure investments.

Tether Capital made an investment in Stables on Nov. 17, which is developing payment infrastructure based on the USDT. According to Tether, the platform allows businesses to capture, transform and transact payments in various markets.

Tether Capital had already injected $15 million into fintech Nomad, which offers dollar accounts, global transactions, investments, into a Brazilian company one day earlier. The companies are also looking into potential integrations based on USDT and Tether Gold.

Together, the investments show Tether pushing stablecoins beyond crypto trading and deeper into institutional settlement, treasury operations and cross-border payments.

title: Washington Politics Are Crushing Crypto Industry Ambitions, Warns Bitwise CIO
summary: Matt Hougan, CIO of Bitwise, a multibillion-dollar crypto and onchain finance investment firm, believes that crypto will be unable to fulfill its promise of upgrading the system while being kneecapped by regulations stopping it from implementing the necessary changes for innovation.   Bitwise CEO La...
content:
1. News
  2. Crypto News
  3. Washington Politics Are Crushing Crypto Industry Ambitions, Warns Bitwise CIO

Published:Nov 21, 2026, 11:55 AM EST

Matt Hougan, CIO of Bitwise, a multibillion-dollar crypto and onchain finance investment firm, believes that crypto will be unable to fulfill its promise of upgrading the system while being kneecapped by regulations stopping it from implementing the necessary changes for innovation.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 21, 2026, 11:55 AM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan argues strict regulations are crippling crypto’s real-world financial utility.
  • He cited stablecoins, claiming bank lobbying prevents them from paying interest and gaining market share.
  • Hougan stressed that navigating Washington hurdles has slowed innovation, risking crypto’s public mindshare.

Bitwise CEO Laments Crypto Industry’s Regulatory Woes

Facing the current market drawdown, some crypto executives are still examining the value of digital assets in real-world applications—and how they have been unable to fulfill the promise of revolutionizing finance.

Matt Hougan, CIO of Bitwise Asset Management, a crypto-focused investment firm that manages billions of dollars’ worth of assets for its customers, has given his take on the state of the crypto system and how its original purpose has been stopped by regulatory concerns.

On social media, Hougan stressed that it was very difficult for crypto to implement real change while being tied up by regulators.

“One problem for crypto is that we’re trying to prove real-world utility while having our best features kneecapped,” he declared.

To illustrate his point, Hougan explained how one of the most extended use cases of cryptocurrency, dollar-pegged stablecoins, are a prime example of these constraints, being restrained as a result of the attack of big banks.

“The best example is stablecoins, which are fighting for market share while not being allowed to pay interest as a sop to the banking lobby,” Hougan assessed.

The issue of stablecoin yields was one of the unsolved problems that analysts claim brought the CLARITY Act down, as community banks complained about the effect that yield-paying stablecoins would have on their deposits.

Other activities involving tokenized stocks, an area where crypto is also facing opposition from large public companies, can also prop up the real-world utility of cryptocurrency.

Hougan mentions that in France, stockholders who commit to hold their shares for long-term periods are rewarded with higher dividends, but that the paperwork to achieve this is complex.

“Crypto could make it easy. I suspect firms would be lining up for the tokenized stock exemption if they could reward long-term shareholders and work against short-sellers in the new format,” he acknowledged.

Finally, Hougan recognized that the ongoing process of introducing regulated crypto features to the current financial system has slowed down the rate and scope of these innovations.

“We’ve been so worn down by negotiating in Washington that we’ve lost some ambition to radically upgrade the system. I understand it, but it’s frustrating,” he concluded, adding that crypto should strive to improve the U.S. system or risk losing the battle for public mindshare.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Bitcoin Hits $55,500 following Strategy’s Massive $16.8B Paper Loss
summary:
Key Takeaways: The price of Bitcoin sank to $55,500 on November 20, marking the lowest price since September 2024. The amount of Bitcoin that Strategy had in its possession was
The post Bitcoin Hits $55,500 following Strategy’s Massive $16.8B Paper Loss appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The price of Bitcoin sank to $55,500 on November 20, marking the lowest price since September 2024.
  • The amount of Bitcoin that Strategy had in its possession was $16.8 billion less than what they paid for it.
  • Strategy kept its Bitcoin buying spree with 485 more BTC valued at $33.4 million, while maintaining a cash cushion of $4.75 billion.

The recent drop has put a strain on corporate Bitcoin holders as Strategy is left with a significant valuation difference between when they acquired the Bitcoins and today’s market prices. The crypto sell-off dropped the digital asset under $56,000, drawing the eyes of the cryptocurrency community back to the company’s massive digital asset reserves.

JUST IN:

Michael Saylor (@saylor)’s #Strategy is down $16.9B on 850,849 $BTC($47.3B).

Tom Lee (@fundstrat)’s #Bitmine is down $11B on 6,077,745 $ETH ($9.35B). https://t.co/bIzwIkJDG9

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 21, 2026

  • Bitcoin Falls to Its Lowest Level since September 2024
  • Strategy’s Unrealized Bitcoin Loss Reaches $16.8 Billion
  • Strategy Continues Buying Bitcoin despite Mounting Losses

Bitcoin Falls to Its Lowest Level since September 2024

The price of Bitcoin on Coinbase closed Friday, November 20, at $55,500, the lowest price since September 2024. According to trading data, the cryptocurrency hit this price at the one minute mark of the minute that started at 11:07 p.m. ET.

The drop was also seen on Bitstamp, which saw Bitcoin hit $55,483.28 just a short while later. The agreement between the two exchanges was a reflection on the severity and magnitude of the market crash.

Bitcoin was then trading at $55,726.26 on Coinbase at 12:56 a.m. ET on November 21. The price is up just a bit, but remains 10.4% off a record low from November 14, 2018, when it reached $61,946.17.

The recent dip also increased the gap between Bitcoin’s price and it’s all time high of $126,080, which was recorded in October 2025. The cryptocurrency is now around 56% off that record as it has lost a lot of its gains.

Read More: $72.3B Bitcoin Giant Strategy Fuels Fresh Buy Rumors with Saylor’s Latest Post

Strategy’s Unrealized Bitcoin Loss Reaches $16.8 Billion

Strategy’s large Bitcoin treasury has made the company particularly exposed to the ongoing price decline.

The November 16 disclosure stated that Strategy’s holdings of Bitcoin as of November 15 totaled 850,849 BTC. The company had spent about $64.20 billion building up those assets, and the average cost of acquisition (including fees and costs) was $75,452 per Bitcoin.

Bitcoin traded around 26% lower at $55,726.26. As per the disclosures, the estimated loss for Strategy was around $16.8 billion as unrealized losses. This is the amount of money it has made or lost on its BTC investment compared to the purchase price. It does not represent an actual loss from selling the assets.

Strategy Continues Buying Bitcoin despite Mounting Losses

Even as the gross shortfall increased, Strategy has been steadily increasing its Bitcoin holdings. The company bought additional 485 BTC during the period from November 9 to November 15 that cost around $33.4 million. The purchase is made with proceeds of common-stock sales.

In addition, Strategy said it has $4.75 billion in cash in the U.S. dollar equivalent in reserve as of November 15. The money is to be used to pay the dividends on preferred stock and the interest on its debts.

These numbers should be taken into consideration when looking at the company’s financial status during the downturn. Its Bitcoin reserves have declined significantly from their acquisition price, but Strategy still has a dedicated cash reserve to cover its financial obligations.
