title: Trump Pushes AI Data Centers Tax to Keep Jobs in US While Calling for Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Comeback
summary: President Donald Trump has proposed penalizing US companies that build AI data centers overseas while urging Nvidia to bring back former chief executive Jensen Huang.
content:
Skip to content

President Donald Trump has proposed penalizing US companies that build AI data centers overseas while urging Nvidia to bring back former chief executive Jensen Huang.

The comments, made during a White House press conference on November 20, highlight two priorities for the administration: keeping artificial intelligence infrastructure within the United States and maintaining its competitive position against China.

Trump Proposes Tax on Overseas AI Data Centers

Trump said his administration would prevent American companies from establishing data centers outside the country or impose a substantial financial penalty on those that proceed. Referring to the proposed measure, he warned that companies building facilities abroad would face a “tremendous tax.”

President Trump proposed a hefty tax on US AI firms building data centers overseas to protect domestic infrastructure and jobs amid growing competition with China. Source: @SkyNews/X

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said during the press conference.

The president argued that allowing critical technology infrastructure and manufacturing operations to move overseas could weaken America’s position in the global AI race. He pointed to the semiconductor industry as an example, suggesting that the United States had fallen behind after allowing chip production to expand abroad.

The proposal reflects Trump’s broader effort to attract investment, infrastructure development, and technology-related employment to the domestic market. However, he did not provide a proposed tax rate, implementation schedule, or details about which companies and projects would fall under the measure.

The announcement also came with questions about its legal and administrative feasibility. According to Axios, Trump acknowledged that he had not discussed the proposal with his officials before making the announcement. The president also did not explain whether he would seek congressional approval or attempt to use existing executive powers.

The US Constitution grants Congress authority to impose federal taxes, leaving the precise legal route for Trump’s proposed measure unresolved. No formal legislative framework or implementing regulations were outlined during the announcement.

Domestic Data Center Expansion Faces Public Opposition

Trump’s proposal comes as the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure faces growing resistance in several US communities. Although the administration wants companies to build more facilities domestically, the projects have generated concerns about electricity consumption, water requirements, and their potential impact on household utility costs.

Data centers require substantial computing capacity to train and operate increasingly sophisticated AI models. Their electricity demand can place additional pressure on local power networks, while cooling systems can require significant water resources. These issues have become prominent subjects in local planning discussions and election campaigns.

The backlash also became a political issue during the 2026 midterm election cycle, with voters considering measures to restrict or impose additional conditions on data center development. Consequently, Trump’s effort to discourage overseas construction comes at a time when some American communities are questioning the costs of hosting these facilities.

There is also an economic consideration. Data center operators frequently establish facilities close to customers to reduce processing delays and the expense of transmitting large volumes of information. For companies serving international clients, maintaining infrastructure across different countries can therefore remain important.

A policy that increases the cost of overseas construction could influence future investment decisions by US technology firms. However, its ultimate impact would depend on the scope of the proposed tax and whether companies receive any exemptions.

Trump Highlights AI Competition With China

Trump linked his data center proposal to the wider competition between Washington and Beijing over artificial intelligence. During the same press conference, he discussed his recent Asia trip and his conversations with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Morgan Stanley is projecting capacity to climb from 48 GW in 2026 to 117 GW by 2030. Source: @MojoTricks/X

The president claimed that he and Xi had agreed to establish “joint guardrails” for AI development. He did not explain what those safeguards would involve or whether they would lead to any formal agreement between the two governments.

Trump also described artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” arguing that the United States remained ahead of China in the race to develop the technology. He presented the competition as largely revolving around the two countries, with China occupying second place in his assessment.

The comments come amid continuing US efforts to restrict China’s access to advanced computing technology. The Commerce Department has moved to tighten controls on advanced AI chip exports to several Southeast Asian countries to prevent the technology from reaching Chinese companies through third-party channels.

Data centers have become part of this broader technology competition because they allow businesses to access powerful processors and computing resources without necessarily purchasing the hardware themselves. Reuters has reported that Chinese companies have continued accessing computing capacity through overseas data centers in countries permitted to receive advanced chips.

This creates a connection between Trump’s proposed tax and the administration’s semiconductor policies. Both approaches seek to protect America’s technological position while limiting the channels through which China can access advanced AI computing resources.

Trump Calls for Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia

Alongside his comments about AI infrastructure, Trump renewed his support for Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia chief executive.

Huang resigned from his positions as president, CEO, and board member on November 12, 2026, following reports involving alleged extramarital relationships. Nvidia’s board subsequently appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while beginning the search for a permanent replacement.

President Trump called on Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, urging it to accept his apology and give him another opportunity. Source: @wallstengine/X

Trump described Huang as one of the most talented figures in the technology industry and argued that Nvidia should consider giving him another opportunity to lead the company.

“I would love to see him back,” Trump said, adding that Huang should “be given a second chance.”

The president also suggested that Nvidia should accept an apology from its former chief executive and allow him to return to work. He credited Huang with helping develop the company’s advanced Blackwell AI chip platform, which has become an important part of its computing business.

Trump further argued that Huang’s technical contributions had helped put the United States significantly ahead in AI chip development. His remarks reflected concern about losing an executive whose work has been closely associated with Nvidia’s expansion in the global semiconductor industry.

The comments followed an earlier wave of support for Huang from technology industry figures and investors. Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney were among those who backed a petition calling for Nvidia to reconsider the decision while an independent investigation proceeds.

Nvidia Board Maintains Leadership Transition

Despite Trump’s public backing, Huang’s return to Nvidia does not appear to be part of the board’s current plans. The Associated Press reported that a person familiar with the board’s thinking said directors were not considering reinstating the former CEO.

The circumstances surrounding Huang’s resignation remain sensitive. Reports described alleged relationships with a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him and a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of having connections to Beijing. The latter allegation has not been publicly established as fact, and Trump has questioned whether the woman was a spy.

The issue has also raised questions about corporate governance, executive conduct, and potential national security concerns. Nvidia’s board now faces the task of maintaining confidence among investors, employees, and customers while the company searches for permanent leadership.

The administration itself has shown differing views on the company’s future. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent previously called for a significant leadership shake-up and suggested that Nvidia should consider an external candidate. Trump’s endorsement of Huang’s return therefore contrasts with Bessent’s stated preference for a different leadership direction.

For now, Colette Kress remains responsible for Nvidia’s executive leadership while the board considers potential successors. The company has said it expects operations, customer commitments, and its product roadmap to continue without interruption.

Trump’s two announcements highlight the administration’s growing focus on the strategic importance of AI infrastructure and semiconductor leadership. However, the proposed overseas data center tax still lacks an implementation framework, while Huang’s potential return depends on a decision by Nvidia’s board rather than presidential support alone.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Hong Kong has published a bill to expand crypto licensing requirements to custody, advisory, dealing and management services under the SFC’s oversight. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since July amid a broader selloff in US stocks, while European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde warned that differing rules could fragment Europe’s tokenized securities markets.

Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules

Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration, extending oversight beyond trading platforms.

On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing to regulate four activities, including virtual asset dealing, advisory, management and custody. Firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from or register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

The proposed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would subject providers to fit-and-proper checks and other regulatory requirements. Banks and stored-value facility licensees supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also have to register with the SFC to offer virtual asset services.

SFC chief executive Julia Leung said the proposal would strengthen investor protections and provide clearer paths for responsible innovation. The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

In October, Hong Kong said it would introduce legislation covering those four activities before the end of 2026, following consultations on the proposed framework.

The expanded regime has raised implementation concerns. In January, the Hong Kong Securities & Futures Professionals Association warned that introducing licenses without transitional arrangements could force existing businesses to suspend operations while their applications are reviewed. The association called for a six- to 12-month grace period.

Bitcoin falls below $60K for first time since July amid broader market selloff

Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, extending its recent losses amid a broader selloff in technology stocks and other risk assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) had fallen as low as $58,811 before recovering slightly to trade around $59,503, down 5.6% over the past 24 hours as of 16:52 UTC on Friday, according to CoinGecko data. The cryptocurrency has fallen 13.8% over the past week and nearly 30% over the past month.

The decline came amid a broader selloff in US equities. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 5.28% at 22,617.73, while the S&P 500 fell 3.69% to 6,910.77 on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance.

Shares of Anthropic (ANT), which made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, closed down 8.50% at $88.91 amid concerns over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector.

Lagarde warns Europe could miss chance to unify tokenized markets

European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde warned Friday that Europe needs common rules for tokenized securities before incompatible standards take hold across trading platforms.

Speaking at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress, Lagarde said blockchain technology lets firms issue, trade and settle securities on a single platform. The global markets for tokenized assets was worth about 23 billion euros in March, five times its size a year earlier, she said.

Europe could build a single market for those assets, Lagarde said, but if platforms adopt different rules as they grow, they may be unable to settle trades with one another. She said lawmakers have a role alongside the ECB.

“Common rules will be needed too, and those lie with legislators,” she said.

The Eurosystem launched Pontes in September, giving financial institutions a way to settle tokenized securities trades in central bank money. Earlier in November, the European Stability Mechanism used Pontes to settle a 1 billion euro (about $1.1 million) digital bond.

Through a second project, Appia, the Eurosystem is working with market participants on common standards for tokenized securities. It plans to publish a blueprint in 2028.

title: ECB seeks industry partners for tokenized deposits, securities experiments
summary: Industry groups have until Dec. 11 to apply for the ECB’s first experimental exercises under its Appia initiative, with later submissions reviewed on a rolling basis.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 21, 2026

Industry groups have until Dec. 11 to apply for the ECB’s first experimental exercises under its Appia initiative, with later submissions reviewed on a rolling basis.

The European Central Bank (ECB) is seeking financial market participants to help explore tokenized deposits and securities as part of its efforts to build an integrated European financial ecosystem using blockchain technology.

On Friday, the ECB invited industry groups to participate in analytical work and experiments under its Appia initiative, identifying three priority areas, including tokenized deposits and related payments, tokenized securities and shared network governance.

According to the ECB, interested participants must apply as part of a collective initiative comprising independent legal entities rather than individually. Groups can apply for one or more workstreams, with proposals evaluated based on factors including expertise, practical experience, technical readiness and expected contributions.

Applications for the first experimental exercises are due by Dec. 11, while later submissions will be assessed on a rolling basis.

The initiative builds on the Eurosystem’s broader Appia roadmap, which aims to develop a unified European tokenized financial ecosystem anchored in central bank money. The ECB plans to publish a blueprint outlining findings and a proposed framework in 2028.

The invitation comes as ECB President Christine Lagarde warned that Europe risks missing an opportunity to establish an integrated market for tokenized securities if incompatible standards emerge across platforms.

Lagarde urged policymakers to establish common rules to prevent fragmentation as blockchain-based financial infrastructure develops across the region.

summary:

a partne...
content:
The forex and trading industry saw a series of ownership changes, business restructurings and regulatory developments this week. FXCM's ongoing breakup continued to reshape the institutional and retail brokerage landscape, while another broker moved to expand its US futures offering through a partnership with Kraken owner Payward.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Elsewhere, eToro reportedly prepared further workforce reductions, while XTB shares suffered their steepest daily decline since 2021 after Poland's regulator signalled new restrictions on CFDs. Regulators in New Zealand and Europe also brought fresh attention to retail investor protection and the rules governing leveraged trading.

The week also brought developments in proprietary trading, cryptocurrency and the growing relationship between financial firms and professional football. Anthropic's record-breaking IPO attracted considerable interest from trading platforms, but crypto exchanges struggled to secure enough underlying shares for tokenised offerings.

JT Prime to Onboard FXCM's Non-UK Institutional Clients

FXCM Pro will terminate services to its non-UK institutional clients on 18 December, offering them the option to migrate to JT Prime, Finance Magnates reported exclusively. The arrangement will allow clients to retain the same leverage, fees and connectivity conditions after the transfer.

The move follows the sale of FXCM's retail operations, with Trade Nation acquiring its UK client book and AvaTrade purchasing most of its other businesses.

JT Prime, founded by industry veterans Raj Sitlani, Jonathan Brewer and Jeff Wilkins, provides liquidity services to brokers, funds and other professional clients.

Wilkins said the addition of FXCM Pro's institutional clients would support the company's growth. JT Prime is also seeking regulatory approval in a major Western jurisdiction, although its application remains pending.

Broker Client Books Become a Target for Acquisitions

A series of brokerage acquisitions has brought renewed attention to the value of existing client books. Recent transactions include Trade Nation and AvaTrade acquiring parts of FXCM, Capital.com purchasing FxPro's European clients, and CXM Group taking over TD Markets' African business, which included around 50,000 clients.

The deals have raised questions about whether brokers could increasingly build client portfolios for resale. However, industry executives point to significant challenges, including regulatory checks, client retention and the quality of acquired accounts.

ATFX Chief Commercial Officer Siju Daniel said historical transactions were priced with attrition of around 50% in mind. Buyers must also consider the cost of KYC checks and whether clients will remain after ownership changes.

MetroTrade Relaunches US Brokerage With Payward Technology

MetroTrade has relaunched its US retail futures brokerage using technology from Payward Services Derivatives, formerly NinjaTrader Connect. The Chicago-based firm has rebuilt its trading platform, account portal and funding process through the partnership with Kraken's parent company.

The offering includes CME Group futures and cryptocurrency derivatives from Coinbase, while prediction markets are planned for a later release. The new platform has become MetroTrade's primary onboarding channel, although existing clients will continue trading through the broker's established clearing firms.

The move follows Payward's expansion of its brokerage technology services to outside firms after acquiring NinjaTrader in 2025. MetroTrade is backed by Andromeda Capital Partners Suisse, the investment firm associated with Tickmill co-founder Ingmar Mattus.

IG Group Plans Office Closures Across Three European Markets

IG Group is planning to close its offices in France, Spain and Italy, potentially affecting around 50 employees, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The company has reportedly informed staff at the three locations about the plans.

An IG spokesperson told Bloomberg that the broker was consolidating its European operations into a smaller number of larger hubs. The closures form part of a wider organisational restructuring at the London-listed company.

In September, reports emerged that IG was preparing to cut hundreds of jobs as it combined regional consumer operations into a single division. The latest changes follow previous workforce reductions, including a 10% cut in global headcount in 2023. IG had not provided further details by publication time.

eToro Reportedly Prepares Second Round of Layoffs in 12 Months

eToro is planning another round of workforce reductions that could affect dozens of employees globally, Israeli media outlet Calcalist reported. The cuts could take place in the coming weeks, marking the company's second reported layoff exercise within 12 months.

In January, the fintech reduced its workforce by approximately 7%, or around 105 employees. The latest report comes after eToro recorded weaker third-quarter financial results in 2026, with net income falling 74% year-on-year to $15 million.

Net contribution declined 13% to $186 million. The company also reported a significant drop in cryptocurrency activity, with clients placing two million crypto trades in October, down 62% from a year earlier. eToro had not confirmed the reported cuts by publication time.

XTB Shares Suffer Worst Daily Decline Since 2021 on CFD Concerns

XTB shares plunged 17.5% on Tuesday after Poland's financial regulator signalled plans for new restrictions on contracts for difference. The decline was the broker's steepest single-day fall since July 2021, with shares closing at PLN 115.24 after reaching an intraday low of PLN 113.20.

The Polish Financial Supervision Authority's deputy chairman, Dariusz Adamski, said a new product intervention would come soon, although he provided no timetable.

He cited losses of nearly PLN 2 billion among 267,000 Polish CFD clients last year, almost seven times the 2019 figure. CFDs generated 90.5% of XTB's gross result from financial instruments in the third quarter, leaving the broker particularly exposed to potential restrictions.

New Zealand's FMA Introduces Stricter Derivatives Suitability Requirements

New Zealand's Financial Markets Authority (FMA) has introduced stricter suitability requirements for derivatives issuers serving retail clients. From 18 November 2027, firms must collect sufficient information to assess whether a product is appropriate before allowing a client to trade.

The new rules also require brokers to ensure customers understand the products and their associated risks. Firms will not be permitted to allow trading where a product is unsuitable or the investor does not understand it.

The regulator has introduced additional safeguards for providers offering highly leveraged derivatives while retaining access to higher-risk products where appropriate protections exist. The changes follow a consultation launched in June 2024, which included proposals to restrict CFD leverage to 30:1.

Topstep Restricts Access From 13 Countries Over Prop Trading Fraud

Proprietary trading firm Topstep is restricting access for users in 13 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe following what it described as a rise in coordinated fraud. The restrictions include Cambodia, Ethiopia, Serbia and Uzbekistan, and will affect fewer than 1,000 existing traders, according to the firm.

This week, we’ll be restricting access in a handful of countries. This will impact less than 1,000 current Topstep Traders but we want to be transparent with you all about why. Protecting the integrity of our program and the security of our community is our responsibility. Lately we’ve seen a rise in coordinated activity from certain regions, including attempts to bypass ID verification and payment safeguards, and coordinated trading across accounts. We’ve been shutting down the accounts involved, but the activity keeps returning through new profiles and new tactics. Topstep exists to help traders grow and prepare for live markets, and we’ve avoided country-level restrictions wherever possible. Given the recent surge in fraud rings, we’re taking a harder step. Watch our socials for more details about which countries will be impacted and next steps.

— Topstep (@Topstep) November 16, 2026

Topstep said it had identified attempts to bypass identity verification and payment safeguards, alongside coordinated trading across multiple accounts. The company had previously closed accounts involved in the activity, but said the abuse continued through newly created profiles and different tactics.

The firm announced the restrictions on social media on 16 November, describing the decision as a step to protect the integrity of its programme. Coordinated hedging groups and account manipulation have become wider concerns across the proprietary trading industry.

Anthropic Raises $81.3 Billion in Record IPO as Trading Interest Surges

Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in its initial public offering, making it the largest IPO on record. The artificial intelligence company priced its shares at $83 each and increased the offering to 980 million shares, valuing the business at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The listing ended more than six months of trading activity involving brokers, banks and cryptocurrency platforms that offered exposure to Anthropic before its shares became publicly available.

Finance Magnates identified more than 90 firms offering related products, including CFDs, perpetual contracts and tokenised shares. Several instruments traded above the IPO price ahead of the listing. A perpetual contract on Hyperliquid's trade.xyz platform was priced at $100.70 on the morning of the debut, around 21% above the offer price.

Crypto Exchanges Struggle to Secure Anthropic Shares for Tokenised IPOs

Cryptocurrency exchanges struggled to fulfil demand for tokenised Anthropic shares, forcing major platforms to refund customers after failing to secure sufficient underlying stock. Binance Wallet returned the funds committed to its campaign after obtaining only 2,957 tokenised shares through xStocks.

Due to circumstances outside of our control, the allocation for the Anthropic xStocks IPO Campaign on Binance Wallet was not ideal. 🔸All participating users’ USDC will be fully returned from the relevant smart contract to their Binance Wallet. 🔸 An allocation totaling roughly 2,957 Anthropic tokenized stocks, will be airdropped pro rata, based on each user's share of the total subscription, to their Binance Wallet addresses at no cost. 🔸 In addition, $1,000,000 worth of bStocks Anthropic tokens (ANTB) will be airdropped to users who applied for a subscription, with a minimum of about 6 USDC worth guaranteed for each eligible participant, and the remainder distributed pro rata based on each user's share of the total subscription. Thank you for your patience and support. For more details, please refer to the announcement👇 https://t.co/kYf06cppeQ

— Binance Wallet (@BinanceWallet) November 19, 2026

The offering had reached its $500 million USDC subscription cap before closing early on 18 November. Binance subsequently announced that participating customers would receive refunds, with the limited allocation distributed proportionally. It also committed $1 million worth of separate Anthropic-related tokens as compensation.

Bitget took a different approach, securing 153,774 shares directly, although retail allocations remained limited. The difficulties echoed similar problems during SpaceX's IPO in June, when several crypto platforms also failed to obtain enough shares to meet demand.

EU Rejects Retail Investment Strategy but CFD Brokers Face Further Risks

The European Parliament rejected the Retail Investment Strategy (RIS) Omnibus Directive on 12 November, voting 300 to 286, with 23 abstentions. The decision halted proposed changes covering client categorisation, inducements and financial marketing, providing temporary relief for CFD brokers and their affiliate networks.

However, the Parliament approved a separate amendment to the PRIIPs regulation by 311 to 261. The rejected directive would have introduced stricter value-for-money requirements and greater responsibility for firms over marketing communications, including content distributed through financial influencers.

NAGA's Senior Regional Director Alexandru Badea warned that the rejection does not remove the regulatory risks facing CFD providers. National regulators could introduce their own restrictions, potentially creating different requirements across European markets. Poland's planned CFD intervention further illustrates that pressure on brokers remains.

Brokers and Trading Firms Expand Premier League Sponsorship Deals

Trading platforms and financial firms are increasing their presence in Premier League football as gambling companies lose access to front-of-shirt sponsorships. The change, which took effect this season, created an opening for brokers and investment firms seeking greater brand visibility among football audiences.

eToro, Trade Nation, Marex, Plus500, EC Markets and Spreadex are among the companies using football partnerships. eToro has agreements with Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Leeds United, while Marex became Nottingham Forest's global markets partner earlier this year. Trade Nation also maintains a partnership with Aston Villa.

The deals offer firms access to club audiences, hospitality and marketing opportunities. However, the Financial Conduct Authority has warned clubs about sponsorship arrangements involving unauthorised financial services providers, highlighting the compliance considerations surrounding these partnerships.

title: US lawmakers propose up to 30% rewards for prediction market whistleblowers
summary: Whistleblowers could receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases exceeding $1 million in penalties.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 21, 2026

Whistleblowers could receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases exceeding $1 million in penalties.

Two US lawmakers have proposed paying whistleblowers up to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases, seeking tips about suspected insider trading.

On Friday, Democratic Representatives Sean Casten and Ted Lieu announced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026. The bill would establish a Department of Justice program rewarding people whose original information helps resolve enforcement actions.

Under the proposal, whistleblowers would receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions from covered federal fraud cases involving prediction market platforms, provided that the sanctions exceed $1 million. The rewards would come from the DOJ’s Assets Forfeiture Fund, with the Attorney General determining payouts based on the significance of information and assistance.

The bill would permit anonymous submissions through lawyers and prohibit employer retaliation against whistleblowers.

The lawmakers cited concerns about government insiders profiting from bets on military operations and presidential speeches, including on platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.

The latest proposal follows Senate passage of the DEATH BETS Act on Thursday, which would prohibit federally regulated prediction markets from offering contracts tied to war, assassination, terrorism and death.

In March, lawmakers introduced separate legislation to prevent officials from using nonpublic information to trade prediction market contracts. In May, House lawmakers sought records from Kalshi and Polymarket over suspected insider trading linked to military actions.

title: Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules
summary: Hong Kong’s securities regulator says the proposal would strengthen investor protections, with the bill set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 21, 2026

Hong Kong’s securities regulator says the proposal would strengthen investor protections, with the bill set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration, extending oversight beyond trading platforms.

On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing to regulate four activities, including virtual asset dealing, advisory, management and custody. Firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from or register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

The proposed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would subject providers to fit-and-proper checks and other regulatory requirements. Banks and stored-value facility licensees supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also have to register with the SFC to offer virtual asset services.

SFC chief executive Julia Leung said the proposal would strengthen investor protections and provide clearer paths for responsible innovation. The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

In October, Hong Kong said it would introduce legislation covering those four activities before the end of 2026, following consultations on the proposed framework.

The expanded regime has raised implementation concerns. In January, the Hong Kong Securities & Futures Professionals Association warned that introducing licenses without transitional arrangements could force existing businesses to suspend operations while their applications are reviewed. The association called for a six- to 12-month grace period.

title: Crypto News Today: Bitcoin Price Nears $55K as Ethereum Plunges 10% and XRP Tests $0.87 Support
summary: Bitcoin fell to $56,813.68 in a late-Friday snapshot, while Ethereum dropped nearly 10% and XRP traded just above its $0.87 technical support level.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Bitcoin fell to $56,813.68 in a late-Friday snapshot, while Ethereum dropped nearly 10% and XRP traded just above its $0.87 technical support level.

The November 21 selloff has kept all three cryptocurrencies under pressure, with moving averages indicating sustained bearish momentum. Although oversold readings suggest that selling pressure could ease temporarily, the broader technical picture remains negative. Investors are watching whether Bitcoin can stabilize below $60,000, Ethereum can defend the $1,550–$1,580 area, and XRP can avoid another test of its recent lows.

Bitcoin Price Nears $55K as Bearish Signals Strengthen

Bitcoin (BTC) remains under significant selling pressure after falling below $60,000 for the first time since July. Reuters reported that BTC declined 9.67% to $55,809 at 03:50 GMT on November 21. The latest move followed a broader retreat in risk assets, with concerns about elevated valuations weighing on the artificial intelligence trade and other market segments.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The technical picture also points to continued weakness. The TradingView analysis recorded 16 sell signals, seven neutral readings, and only three buy signals across its combined indicators. Moving averages were particularly bearish, with 14 sell signals, one neutral reading, and no buy signals. This alignment suggests that Bitcoin’s downtrend extends beyond a short-term price correction.

Several momentum indicators reinforce that assessment. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) on the 14-day setting stood at 18, indicating deeply oversold conditions. The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) reached -127, while Williams Percent Range fell to -93. These readings suggest that selling may be approaching exhaustion, although they do not independently establish a price reversal.

Meanwhile, the MACD remained negative at -5,033, and the Momentum indicator registered -15,050. Both readings point to persistent downward pressure. The Average Directional Index (ADX) at 46 also indicates a strong prevailing trend, supporting the view that the bearish structure remains firmly established.

Bitcoin’s moving averages provide further evidence of the weakness. The 10-day exponential and simple moving averages stood near $64,088 and $64,125, respectively. Longer-term averages were positioned considerably higher, with the 50-day EMA near $73,842 and the 200-day EMA around $75,217. These levels represent potential recovery barriers if buyers attempt to regain control.

The supplied classic pivot analysis identified $58,181 as an important support reference. However, with the later Bitcoin quote already below that level, traders need to reassess the pivot structure against updated price data. On the upside, the $64,000 area represents an initial resistance zone based on the short-term moving averages.

Ethereum Price Plunges Over 10% as $1,543 Support Comes Into Focus

Ethereum (ETH) experienced an even sharper decline, with one CoinGlass market snapshot showing the cryptocurrency at $1,543.46, down 10.69% over 24 hours. Its recorded intraday range extended from $1,539.90 to $1,762.80. A subsequent market update showed ETH recovering toward $1,618, illustrating how quickly prices have moved during the selloff.

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The TradingView technical analysis classified Ethereum’s overall position as Strong Sell. The combined indicator summary recorded 16 sell signals and 10 neutral readings, with no buy signals. Moving averages accounted for 14 sell signals and one neutral reading, while the oscillator group remained predominantly neutral.

Ethereum’s momentum indicators also reflect the scale of the decline. The 14-day RSI stood at 18.9, placing it well below the traditional oversold threshold of 30. The Stochastic %K reached 6.8, while the CCI registered -133.8. These readings indicate substantial downward pressure and the possibility of a temporary recovery if selling activity slows.

However, the MACD at -170.8 and Momentum indicator at -450.1 continued to generate sell signals. The ADX reading of 41.7 suggests that the prevailing trend remains strong rather than reflecting ordinary sideways price movement. As a result, the oversold readings have not yet provided sufficient confirmation of a bullish reversal.

Ethereum is also trading considerably below its key moving averages. The 10-day EMA and SMA stood near $1,833 and $1,838, respectively, while the 20-day EMA was positioned around $1,975. The 50-day EMA near $2,181 and 200-day EMA around $2,262 highlight the distance ETH would need to recover before its broader technical structure begins to improve.

The $1,550–$1,580 area is an important near-term zone to monitor, given the recent trading range. A sustained move below this region could expose Ethereum to further losses. Conversely, the Hull Moving Average near $1,697 represents an initial recovery hurdle, followed by resistance around the $1,833–$1,838 moving-average cluster.

XRP Price Tests $0.87 Support as Oversold Readings Emerge

XRP (XRP) has also experienced persistent selling, with the price falling below the $1.00 level and approaching an important technical support region. A previous technical snapshot placed XRP near $0.8710, while subsequent market data showed the token recovering toward $0.91. Its November 20 trading session recorded a low around $0.865, keeping the $0.87 support zone in focus.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The broader trend remains bearish despite some improvements in short-term momentum readings. The TradingView daily technical assessment showed a Sell rating, while the hourly, four-hour, and weekly timeframes also leaned toward Sell or Strong Sell. This reflects the pressure affecting XRP across multiple trading periods.

The 14-day RSI stood near 25.42, indicating oversold conditions. The Stochastic %K was around 11.97, while Williams Percent Range reached approximately -92.46. These readings suggest that XRP has experienced substantial selling and could enter a consolidation phase if buyers return.

However, its moving averages continue to indicate a weak market structure. The 10-day simple moving average was near $0.9618, while the corresponding exponential average stood around $0.9727. Longer-term averages were positioned substantially higher, including the 50-day SMA near $1.24 and the 100-day SMA around $1.31.

The MACD and Momentum indicators also remained negative, highlighting the difference between short-term oversold conditions and the broader downward trend.

Classic pivot calculations identify $0.8718 as the first notable support level, followed by $0.8343 and $0.7469. On the upside, the central pivot sits near $0.9217, with initial resistance around $0.9592. A sustained move above these levels would help reduce immediate bearish pressure, while a break below $0.8718 could expose XRP to additional selling.

Crypto Market Outlook: Oversold Conditions Face Persistent Selling Pressure

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP are displaying similar technical characteristics despite differences in their recent price movements. All three assets are trading below their principal moving averages, while negative MACD and momentum readings continue to indicate downward pressure.

The oversold readings across their RSI and other oscillators deserve attention. Bitcoin’s RSI near 18, Ethereum’s at 18.9, and XRP’s around 25.42 suggest that recent selling has pushed momentum toward historically weak territory. Such conditions can precede a temporary rebound, but they do not guarantee that prices have reached a durable bottom.

The key distinction is that moving averages continue to favor sellers. Bitcoin faces recovery barriers beginning around $64,000, Ethereum must reclaim levels near $1,697 and $1,833, while XRP needs to move above its $0.92–$0.96 resistance region to improve its short-term outlook.

For now, the immediate focus remains on price stabilization. Bitcoin’s ability to recover above $60,000, Ethereum’s response around $1,550, and XRP’s defense of the $0.87 region will help determine whether the current decline begins to slow or develops into another leg lower.

The technical readings reflect historical price behavior and can change quickly as new trading data becomes available. Until stronger buying activity and confirmation across multiple timeframes emerge, the broader market structure continues to favor a cautious outlook.

title: Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
The bitcoin price slipped to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, briefly dipping under its summer low, as a chip-led selloff sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and dragged crypto stocks and miners sharply lower.
This post ...
content:
The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low.

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022.

Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower

Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory.

Chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported.

Anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported.

Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price

Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600.

Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record.

Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other growth assets that depend on easy money, he said.

The dip to $57,655 briefly took bitcoin just under its summer low near $57,700. It is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing streak since 2022.

Crypto stocks extend losses

Strategy (MSTR) fell about 8.4% to near $78.90, adding to the losses after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) dropped about 5.5% to near $103. Robinhood (HOOD) lost about 9.6% and Circle (CRCL) fell about 7.9%.

Bitcoin miners fared worst. MARA Holdings (MARA) sank about 17% to near $5.17, IREN (IREN) fell about 17% and CleanSpark (CLSK) dropped about 16%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 8.4%, and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) fell about 9.4%. Many miners have expanded into AI data centers, tying their shares to the chip selloff.

The bitcoin price is now down more than 50% from its record above $126,000, set in October 2025.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $58,300.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Anthropic’s Two-Tier Debut: Who Got $83 Shares and Who Financed the $111.50 Open
summary:
Anthropic invited retail investors to participate in its historic IPO, but most retail traders faced the brick wall of geo and eligibility restrictions, becoming the exit liquidity for the opening pop. 
Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83 each before trading began under the ANT ticker o...
content:
2026-11-20T21:50:25.673+02:00

Friday, 20/11/2026 | 19:50 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Broker eligibility rules and geographic exclusions split retail investors during Anthropic’s debut.
  • Vanda Research tracked a record $700M–$800M in debut-day retail volume against just $60M in net buying.

Anthropic invited retail investors to participate in its historic IPO, but most retail traders faced the brick wall of geo and eligibility restrictions, becoming the exit liquidity for the opening pop.

Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83 each before trading began under the ANT ticker on 19 November.

The company allocated 15% of the offering to retail accounts, but eventually millions of self-directed traders across excluded jurisdictions and brokerages were forced to wait for Nasdaq’s opening bell.

Those secondary-market buyers entered as the stock opened 34% higher at $111.50, only to absorb an immediate 13% intraday drawdown as shares faded to close at $97.17.

Retail Investors Were Geo-fenced and Condition-Fenced

Several brokers, including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, Trade-PMR, SoFi and Morgan Stanley’s E*TRADE allowed retail clients to participate in Anthropic's initial offering.

However, having an account with a participating broker was not enough to qualify as an IPO investor, as many set blocking conditions.

Thus, at Fidelity, eligible traders should have at least $25,000 in certain assets and subscribe for a minimum of 25 shares - $2,075 at $83 a share.

@Maximo8136151 That's correct. Brokerage clients with at least $25,000 in eligible assets can participate in this initial public offering (IPO). If you have any other questions, don't hesitate to let us know!

— Fidelity Investments (@Fidelity) November 10, 2026

Hargreaves Lansdown took applications from eligible UK clients from day one, with a minimum of £250. 45,811 applications were received with an average application of £6,661. Demand was so strong that clients ended up with 33.6% of the shares they requested.

Geo restrictions also applied: the prospectus covered retail investors from the UK, Switzerland, Australia, Canada, Japan and selected EU countries.

Secondary Buyers Absorbed the Post-Open Slide

Activity in the Czech Republic shows how retail investors have reacted in a market excluded from Anthropic's core offering. It also illustrates the prices and risks they faced in getting in after exchange trading began.

Clients of Patria, Fio and XTB entered after Nasdaq trading opened, immediately facing a price 34% above the IPO allocation.

Patria recorded activity from around 500 clients and turnover of approximately CZK100 million. Fio clients traded about $1.5 million, while Anthropic became XTB’s most-traded stock that Thursday, according to ITBiz.

The initial spike didn't last. Anthropic fell from $111.50 to $97.17 by the end of Thursday and traded just above $84 the following session, meaning secondary market buyers got a very different entry point than those who'd been allocated shares in the IPO.

Broader US trading data confirms that the first-day frenzy was driven by intense two-way flipping rather than buy-and-hold accumulation. Total retail turnover - both buy and sell orders - reached an estimated $700 million to $800 million on debut day, according to Vanda Research strategist Viraj Patel, as cited by Bloomberg.

That surpassed SpaceX’s $669 million debut earlier this year to mark the largest single-day retail IPO turnover in Vanda’s dataset dating back to 2012.

Yet net retail buying finished Thursday at roughly $60 million, half of SpaceX’s $118 million net inflow and well below Coinbase’s $92 million debut in 2021, as early holders and day-traders aggressively sold into the $111.50 opening pop while secondary buyers stepped in on the other side.

Pre-IPO CFDs Offered Only Exposure

Several brokers, including Pepperstone, EBC Financial Group, Exness, IC Markets, NAGA, and PU Prime, as well as XTB in select regions, offered pre-IPO CFDs on Anthropic.

Those instruments allowed clients to speculate on indicative valuations before the listing. Clients didn't own any Anthropic shares, didn't have any shareholder rights and didn't get any of the $83 primary allocation price.

The positions were subject to leverage, financing charges, and platform-specific repricing rules once official Nasdaq trading went live.

Anthropic's listing showed that even an estimated $12 billion retail tranche isn't enough to flatten the structural hierarchy of a blockbuster IPO.

Between the various wealth thresholds, the oversubscription rationing and the regional carve-outs, primary access was still a very privileged thing.

The rest of the retail market were simply left with the choice of either paying the $111.50 to get in at the opening peak or trading the synthetic alternatives off the sidelines.

title: Wrapped Monero token crashes 99.8% amid suspected $13.5M exploit
summary: Bitquery traced $13.5 million in suspicious sales of the wrapped Monero token, as its operator blamed a security breach and promised to reimburse affected traders.
content:
A wrapped version of Monero (XMR) plunged more than 99% on Hyperliquid on Friday after a wallet that received tokens from the deployer account sold approximately $13.5 million worth of the asset, according to blockchain analytics firm Bitquery.

The token, known as XMR1, fell from around $500 to $1 in roughly 30 minutes, a 99.8% decline, according to Bitquery. Wrapped tokens are designed to represent other cryptocurrencies on different blockchains, allowing them to be traded outside their native networks. The collapse affected XMR1 rather than Monero’s native cryptocurrency.

According to Bitquery’s onchain analysis, the wallet received 5.2 million XMR1 tokens from the deployer account before selling approximately $13.5 million worth of the asset on Friday.

The firm traced $13.28 million in USDC transferred to Arbitrum, where $13.22 million was exchanged for 7,467 Ether (ETH) through CoW Protocol. Most of the ETH was subsequently bridged to Ethereum.

Bitquery also found that proceeds from four hacks earlier in November, involving Across Protocol, Kava, Lighter and Safe, had been used to purchase approximately $6.6 million worth of XMR1, apparently as a route to native Monero. The firm said it found no onchain evidence linking those incidents to Friday’s suspected exploit.

Value of XMR1 purchases linked to funds from four November hacks. Source: Bitquery

Bitquery said its onchain investigation could not establish how the deployer account’s private key was obtained or who controlled it during the transfers, leaving the circumstances of the suspected compromise unconfirmed.

Related: Binance hacker moves nearly $600M in ETH, routes funds through THORChain, Chainflip

Wagyu operator blames suspected infrastructure breach

PerpetualCow, the pseudonymous operator of Wagyu, the service behind XMR1, attributed the collapse to an alleged breach of hosting provider 1984, claiming that customer data and internal server files had been exposed.

According to PerpetualCow, the XMR1 deployer key had been stored on a server that was subsequently deleted, but the hosting provider allegedly retained logs and files associated with it.

Source: Perpetual Cow

PerpetualCow also pledged to personally reimburse affected traders and said Wagyu would relaunch at a later date, although no timeline was provided.

Cointelegraph contacted the operator for additional details about the suspected breach and reimbursement plans but had not received a response by publication.

title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
The SEC obtained an asset freeze against Backward Hat Capital and its founders, alleging a $560 million Ponzi scheme sold as AI-driven FX trading funded through crypto. Prosecutors and the CFTC filed parallel cases.
Thi...
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading.

The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme.

Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets.

The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month

According to the SEC’s complaint, Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange.

Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted.

Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase.

Where the money went

The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million.

Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme.

Prosecutors in Manhattan charged Williams and Johnson with securities fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit securities fraud. The FBI arrested Williams in Kokomo, Indiana, and Johnson in Gilbert, Arizona, on Wednesday. Prosecutors put the total raised at more than $600 million.

“As alleged, Phillip Patrick Williams and Devin Allen Johnson promised to use investor funds for profitable foreign exchange currency trading,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Williams and Johnson instead stole hundreds of millions of dollars from their investors for personal expenses and to pay off earlier investors in a Ponzi-like fashion.”

Regulators’ latest crypto fraud cases

The CFTC put the Ponzi at more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants and said defendants kept soliciting money through at least October 2026. Its complaint seeks restitution, disgorgement, civil penalties, trading bans and a permanent injunction. The SEC is seeking injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties.

The case follows other recent enforcement actions tied to crypto-branded fraud. The SEC charged two companies in a $130 million crypto trading scheme last month, and New York sought a $1.37 billion judgment against the operators of the NovaTech Ponzi scheme. In August, the CFTC charged Goliath Ventures with a $400 million bitcoin fraud.

Anne McKinley, acting associate director of the SEC’s Chicago Regional Office, said the promise of “a low-risk, high rate of return on a purportedly complex investment should make all potential investors stop and think before investing their money.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Sky Protocol sees $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals, disputes illicit fund claims
summary: Sky says its USDS stablecoin held its $1 value despite more than $2 billion in withdrawals, as it disputes a report linking the protocol to illicit activity.
content:
Sky Protocol processed more than $2 billion in stablecoin redemptions on Thursday, the same day a CoinDesk investigation linked $518 million in transactions through the protocol to illicit activity.

The withdrawals involved users exchanging Sky’s USDS stablecoin for Circle’s USDC through its Peg Stability Module (PSM), a system that allows users to swap the tokens at a fixed rate.

Sky, which has a total value locked (TVL) of $2.3 billion, said on Friday in a statement that USDS maintained its $1 peg throughout the withdrawals. According to the protocol, the amount of USDC held in the PSM never fell below $800 million and had climbed back above $1.1 billion by Friday.

Sky also challenged the investigation, pointing to a review by Block Analitica, which notably serves as a risk adviser to the Sky ecosystem.

The withdrawals came amid concerns raised by the investigation that Circle could freeze USDC held by Sky, potentially making it harder for users to redeem their stablecoins.

Related: Circle freezes $12.6M of USDC linked to privacy protocol Zama

Sky disputes findings on illicit transactions

CoinDesk’s Nov. 19 report looked at research by blockchain analytics firm Inca Digital, which identified $518 million in transactions involving wallets linked to hackers, sanctioned entities, and other threat actors over a span of five years.

Of that amount, around $101.9 million was linked to North Korean actors, including wallets connected to the February 2025 Bybit hack.

Meanwhile, Block Analitica disputed some parts of the investigation, saying that the $518 million represented less than 0.06% of the more than $960 billion processed through Sky’s peg stability modules.

The firm said about two-thirds of the flagged activity occurred between 2021 and mid-2024 – before Sky introduced its newer LitePSM system.

Block Analitica also questioned the reported links to North Korean threat actors, stating that some wallets were several transactions removed from known addresses and may have belonged to unrelated users.

The firm added that most of the flagged transactions passed through trading services such as 1inch, ParaSwap and MetaMask Swaps, which automatically choose where to route trades.

Sky says reserves remain strong despite withdrawals

The large withdrawals also came amid a sharp drop in the number of USDS tokens in circulation. The supply fell nearly 40% in one day to about 3.2 billion tokens, according to DefiLlama data. However, the stablecoin maintained its $1 value despite the decline.

CoinDesk reported that a wallet linked to crypto exchange Poloniex accounted for a large share of the withdrawals, although it wasn’t clear whether the exchange itself was behind the transactions.

The combined circulating supply of Sky’s USDS and DAI stablecoins fell to $6.11 billion as of Nov. 20, down 37.8% over the past 30 days. Source: Sky Ecosystem Financial Insights

Sky said it held about $9.3 billion in assets backing its stablecoins as of Friday, compared with around $6.11 billion in USDS and DAI in circulation, according to its financial dashboard. The dashboard also showed about $93 million in reserves to help cover potential losses.

Cointelegraph reached out to the Sky Frontier Foundation for comment but had not received a response by publication.

title: Anthropic Stock Price Today: ANT Falls 8% as $500B US Tech Sell-Off Hits AI Stocks
summary: Anthropic shares came under renewed selling pressure on Friday as a broader technology market downturn erased much of the optimism surrounding the company's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ANT

Anthropic shares came under renewed selling pressure on Friday as a broader technology market downturn erased much of the optimism surrounding the company's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.

ANT declined approximately 8% in the latest market snapshot, while semiconductor and artificial intelligence stocks also recorded steep losses. The pullback followed a turbulent first trading session on November 19, when Anthropic briefly reached a $2 trillion market valuation before retreating from its opening gains.

ANT Stock Price Retreats After Strong IPO Debut

Anthropic (ANT) shares faced a sharp correction on November 20, extending the volatility that followed their highly anticipated stock market debut. The company began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 at an initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 per share.

Anthropic Stock (ANT) price chart. Source: @SantimentData/X

Investor demand initially pushed the stock considerably higher. ANT opened at $111.50, representing a 34% premium to its IPO price, and briefly reached a valuation of approximately $2 trillion. However, the initial buying momentum weakened throughout the session, leaving shares at $97.17 at Thursday’s close, still approximately 17% above the offering price.

The following day’s decline reflected growing caution among investors. Reuters reported ANT trading near $88.24 on Friday, approximately 9% below its previous close. The pullback erased a substantial portion of its first-session gains, although the shares remained above their original IPO price.

The scale of Anthropic’s listing also attracted attention. The company initially raised approximately $81.3 billion through its offering. Following the full exercise of the underwriters’ additional share purchase option, Anthropic disclosed that gross IPO proceeds had reached approximately $93.5 billion. A separate $26 billion private placement brought the combined proceeds from both transactions to approximately $119.5 billion.

The opening-day performance initially demonstrated strong demand for exposure to the AI industry. However, the subsequent correction suggests that investors remain selective about valuations, even when a company attracts substantial interest during its public debut.

$500B US Tech Sell-Off Weighs on AI Stocks

Anthropic’s declining share price coincided with an aggressive sell-off across US technology stocks. According to Coin Bureau’s November 20 market update, approximately $500 billion in market capitalization disappeared from US equities within minutes of the opening bell.

US markets suffered a sharp selloff on November 20, wiping out $500 billion in market value as tech and AI stocks tumbled, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.58%. Source: @coinbureau/X

ANT featured among the weakest-performing technology stocks in the update, falling 8.01%. Semiconductor companies also recorded substantial losses, highlighting the extent of the selling pressure across the AI infrastructure sector.

SanDisk declined 8.07%, while Western Digital lost 6.80%. Arm Holdings dropped 6.41%, followed by Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) at 6.32%, Micron Technology at 6.06%, Marvell Technology at 5.97%, and Riot Platforms at 5.30%.

The weakness extended beyond smaller technology companies. Nvidia, Alphabet, and Microsoft also traded lower, with losses of 3.30%, 3.46%, and 1.97%, respectively, in the market snapshot.

The Nasdaq 100 was down 1.58% in the reported snapshot, reflecting renewed pressure on companies closely associated with AI development and semiconductor manufacturing.

Concerns surrounding the sustainability of AI investment have increasingly influenced market sentiment. Investors are questioning whether the enormous capital commitments toward data centers, computing infrastructure, and advanced semiconductor technology can generate sufficient returns.

The broader financial environment has added another layer of uncertainty. Expectations of higher interest rates, rising infrastructure costs, and concerns about AI company valuations have encouraged investors to reassess exposure to growth-oriented technology stocks.

David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, described the changing investment outlook in comments reported by Reuters: “Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth.”

That distinction is important for Anthropic. Its strong IPO demonstrated substantial interest in the company’s business, but the subsequent share-price decline indicates that investor enthusiasm does not necessarily translate into sustained buying pressure across the wider AI sector.

Tokenized Anthropic Shares Draw Attention in Crypto Markets

Anthropic’s public listing also generated significant activity across cryptocurrency platforms, where tokenized securities and derivatives provided additional ways to gain exposure to the company.

Santiment reported a substantial increase in social volume and social dominance surrounding Anthropic tokenization discussions on November 19. Its charts showed simultaneous increases in bullish and bearish mentions, indicating heightened market attention and divided sentiment following the IPO.

Anthropic’s ANT token surged following its $81.3 billion IPO debut before retreating sharply while expanding across multiple blockchains and DeFi platforms. Source: Santiment Intelligence via X

The growing discussion reflects the expansion of tokenized equity products across blockchain networks and decentralized finance platforms. These products allow users to access blockchain-based representations of traditional financial assets, although their structure, trading conditions, and associated risks can differ from those of the underlying shares.

A Glassnode chart also highlighted activity in pre-IPO Anthropic perpetual futures. These contracts reportedly implied valuations between $1.7 trillion and $1.85 trillion during much of the listing week before climbing toward $2 trillion shortly before the Nasdaq debut.

The chart suggests that 24/7 crypto derivatives markets identified Anthropic’s IPO as undervalued, providing more timely pricing signals than traditional banker-set valuations. Source: Glassnode via X

The comparison illustrates how cryptocurrency derivatives markets can reflect changing expectations outside conventional US trading hours. However, futures-based valuations represent trading expectations rather than official company valuations or guaranteed future share prices.

Meanwhile, Binance Wallet announced compensation arrangements for participants in its Anthropic IPO xStocks campaign after encountering allocation problems beyond its control.

The platform confirmed that participating users would receive full refunds of their committed USDC, alongside a proportional distribution of the available tokenized Anthropic shares. Eligible participants were also set to receive an additional $1 million allocation of bStocks Anthropic tokens, identified by the ticker ANTB.

The announcement highlighted continued demand for blockchain-based access to newly listed companies. It also demonstrated the operational challenges that can emerge when subscription demand exceeds the available allocation of an IPO-linked tokenized product.

Overall, Anthropic’s first two trading sessions have exposed a gap between strong initial demand for its shares and the broader market’s willingness to maintain higher valuations for AI companies. The stock’s next direction will depend partly on how investors assess its growth prospects, spending commitments, and ability to sustain confidence as a publicly traded company.

title: Bitcoin falls below $60K for first time since July amid broader market selloff
summary: Bitcoin fell nearly 6% as US stocks declined, with the Nasdaq dropping more than 2% and Anthropic shares losing almost 10%.
content:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, extending its recent losses amid a broader selloff in technology stocks and other risk assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) had fallen to $58,811 before recovering slightly to trade around $59,503, down 5.6% over the past 24 hours as of 16:52 UTC on Friday, according to CoinGecko data. The cryptocurrency has fallen 13.8% over the past week and nearly 30% over the past month.

Source: CoinGecko

The decline came amid a broader selloff in US equities. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 5.28% at 22,617.73, while the S&P 500 fell 3.69% to 6,910.77 on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance.

Shares of Anthropic (ANT), which made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, closed down 8.50% at $88.91 amid concerns over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $582.3 million in net outflows on Thursday, up from $306.5 million the previous day, according to Farside Investors. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals.

AI selloff drives Bitcoin weakness, CoinShares says

Bitcoin’s decline appears to be driven more by the broader selloff in artificial intelligence stocks than by problems specific to the cryptocurrency market, according to James Butterfill, head of research at CoinShares.

Butterfill told Cointelegraph that Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other liquidity-sensitive growth assets, with deteriorating sentiment toward AI stocks spilling into crypto as investors reduce risk. The prospect of interest rates remaining elevated has made the broader selloff more severe, he added.

The Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00% in October, following a quarter-point increase in September. Traders on Polymarket were pricing in a 94% chance of another rate hike by the Fed’s next policy decision on Dec. 9, as of 17:19 UTC on Friday.

Polymarket traders price in 94% chance of another Fed rate hike in 2026. Source: Polymarket

Despite Bitcoin falling below $60,000, Butterfill said the decline has not fundamentally changed his medium-term outlook.

We have been expecting Bitcoin to trade broadly between $60,000 and $90,000 until there is a meaningful change in liquidity or monetary policy, so a temporary move below the bottom of that range is uncomfortable rather than thesis-changing.

Butterfill said Bitcoin could face further short-term losses if the AI selloff deepens, but should benefit relatively quickly if technology stocks stabilize.

Alexander Blume, founder and CEO of digital asset investment firm Two Prime, told Cointelegraph that macroeconomic instability, interest rates, inflation and a lack of Bitcoin-specific catalysts were contributing to the decline.

However, Blume suggested that selling pressure may be nearing an end.

That being said, I think sellers and leverage liquidations are largely exhausted and would not be surprised for BTC to find a bottom soon.

title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
Blockstream researchers published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a hash-based post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the community to review it for flaws.
This post Researc...
content:
Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function.

The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers.

How SHRINCS works

SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both.

Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block.

The risk of a stateful signature

The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size.

Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”

Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”

Researchers ask for review

The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. Kudinov said it has not been sufficiently peer reviewed, and the project’s GitHub repository warns that the documents may contain errors and should not be the sole basis for deploying SHRINCS. “We tried to be careful, but a proof of this size can have mistakes,” he wrote, asking readers to open an issue if they find one.

The team also produced two results that are not specific to SHRINCS: a classical bound for a property called ITSR without reprogramming, and a quadratic quantum bound for undetectability. Kudinov said they also apply to SPHINCS+ and SLH-DSA, the hash-based schemes SHRINCS borrows from, and that they were published as separate papers.

The SHRINCS work lands as quantum risk climbs the agenda. A global securities regulators’ group this week warned that moving blockchains to quantum-resistant cryptography may be especially hard, and researchers recently built a post-quantum defense for the Lightning Network after Bitcoin’s first quantum-safe transaction was shown without a fork.

The draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal for SHRINCS is also open for comment. “We need all the possible feedback — engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said of it. “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.
